Rework round 1 on A5. The tester caught a real defect: your `header` override on `prompt` is wired correctly, but live Playwright measurement shows the `prompt` header still renders at 72px at tablet/desktop, not the 92px your own comment claims. I've traced the root cause myself by reading `index.tsx` — here's the exact fix, three files.

## Root cause (confirmed, not a guess)

In `index.tsx`'s `ZimmDrawerContent`, the `title || boxedHeader` branch (the one `prompt` uses, via `boxedHeader`) renders the close button as a bare `<ZimmButton variant="icon" .../>` with no height applied — a direct flex child of `headerStyles`. Compare the *other* branch (pure floating case, no title/boxedHeader): there, the identical `ZimmButton` is wrapped in `<chakra.div sx={closeButtonStyles}>`, and `closeButtonStyles` (`baseStyle.closeButton` in `zimmDrawer.css.ts`) explicitly sets `height: DRAWER_HEADER_ROW_HEIGHT` (44px, from `zimmDrawerShared.ts`) on that wrapper.

So in the `header` branch, the button's row height is just its own intrinsic size (tester measured 24px), not Figma's 44px `drawer-header-options` row. Your fix's arithmetic (`24px pad + 44px row + 24px pad = 92px`) assumed the 44px row already existed — it doesn't, in this branch. Total ends up `24 + 24 + 24 = 72px`, coincidentally the old value.

This bug is latent everywhere `header` uses `paddingBlock` instead of `minHeight` — every *other* header override (`large`, `xLarge`) uses `minHeight`, which forces the total box height regardless of the button's real size, papering over this exact gap. `prompt` is the first live consumer to actually depend on padding-driven sizing, which is what exposed it.

## The fix — new recipe part, not a `minHeight` workaround

**1. `zimmDrawer.css.ts`:**
- Add `'headerCloseButton'` to the `parts` array (after `'headerTitle'`).
- Add a new baseStyle key:
  ```ts
  headerCloseButton: {
    display: 'flex',
    alignItems: 'center',
    justifyContent: 'center',
    height: DRAWER_HEADER_ROW_HEIGHT,
    flexShrink: 0,
  },
  ```
  Comment it as: gives the close button its own real 44px row inside the in-flow header (title/boxedHeader branch), matching Figma's `drawer-header-options` row exactly — the floating case already gets this via `closeButton`'s own `height: DRAWER_HEADER_ROW_HEIGHT`, this is the same treatment for the boxed case. Note in the comment that this does NOT change rendered output for any `minHeight`-driven header (large/xLarge/small/mobile) — nested `alignItems:center` centering resolves to the identical visual midpoint either way — it only matters for `paddingBlock`-driven sizing (`xLarge`, `prompt`), where no `minHeight` exists to force the total height.
- Also fix the new `prompt.header` comment's consumer list: the tester confirmed only `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer` (Wishlist/Login) is actually affected by the `HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE` change — "Find in Boutique" and the PDP tab drawer pass neither `title` nor `boxedHeader`, so they never render the `header` part at all (floating close button only, unaffected); "Cookies"/"Notify Me" don't exist as built consumers yet. Correct the comment to name only Wishlist/Login.

**2. `zimmDrawerShared.ts`:** update the file-level comment — `DRAWER_HEADER_ROW_HEIGHT` is now shared by three consumers (`closeButton`, `zimmTabs.menu`, and the new `headerCloseButton`), not two.

**3. `index.tsx`:**
- Add `headerCloseButtonStyles: SystemStyleObject;` to `ZimmDrawerContentConfig`.
- Destructure it in `ZimmDrawerContent`'s params.
- In the `title || boxedHeader` branch, wrap the close button:
  ```tsx
  <chakra.div sx={headerCloseButtonStyles}>
    <ZimmButton variant="icon" icon="close" label={t('drawer.close', 'Close')} onClick={onClose} />
  </chakra.div>
  ```
  (replacing the bare `<ZimmButton .../>` currently there — leave the OTHER branch, the pure floating one, untouched).
- In `ZimmDrawer`'s render call, pass `headerCloseButtonStyles={styles.headerCloseButton}` alongside the other style props.

## Verify before reporting back

- `recipeParts.test.ts` reconciles declared `parts` vs `styles.<part>` usage — since you're both declaring and using the new part, this should pass automatically, but confirm.
- Check `zimmDrawer.css.test.ts` and `index.test.tsx` (the A3 test file) for any assertion that would break from the new wrapping div (e.g. exact child-count or structural queries) — read both fully rather than assuming; update only if genuinely necessary.
- Re-run `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run test`, `npm run audit:tokens` — report exact numbers against baseline (tsc clean; 79/1187/0; audit 3 unacknowledged).
- This does NOT fix the separate `small`-variant-desktop-header question the tester raised (whether Wishlist/Login's own desktop header should also reach 92px) — that's out of scope for this rework, a decision Marcel hasn't made yet. Don't touch `small`'s header.

Report back with the diff and gate numbers.

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will process your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

content.description: One-line fix: site?.sfccSiteId ?? site?.id. Corrected test mocks (currently mock an impossible site.id value). Comment-only correction in footer/index.tsx. content.subject: A3 — ZimmDrawer boxedHeader mode (headerless-title)
content.description: Extend ZimmDrawer with a boxedHeader flag on the labelledBy branch: renders the real in-flow header box (matching the title path's structure) with an empty title span instead of the floating position:absolute close button. # Handoff — SFCC-831 + SFCC-689

Branch: `feature/SFCC-831-689_country-language-mismatch`   Base: `2510cea` (develop)   Head: (in progress)

Plan: `./plan.md` · Decisions: `./decisions.md` + `../SFCC-689/decisions.md` · Gate: `./findings.md`

## Steps

| # | What | Commit | Scorer verdict | Rework rounds |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `npm install` (reconciled stale lockfile drift from PR #71, reverted — out of scope, not committed) | *(no commit)* | — | — |
| A1 | `ZimmDrawer`: `prompt` size + narrow-panel width floor | `e539920` | **PASS** (round 1) | 0 |
| A2 | `ZimmDrawer`: localise close-button label via `useUiCopy` | `50f761b` | **PASS** (round 1) | 0 |
| A4 | `ZimmDrawer`: fix `prompt` mobile height (`bottom: 'auto'`) — emerged from Marcel's design review, not the original plan; see "Steps not in the original plan" below | `622ddf8` | **PASS** (round 1) — Design fidelity marked **CONFIRMED**, not the usual pending-human-check, on the strength of two independent live-Chromium measurement passes | 0 |
| A3 | `ZimmDrawer`: `boxedHeader` mode — emerged from Marcel's design review; see "Steps not in the original plan" below | `246d096` | **PASS** (round 1) — Design fidelity **UNVERIFIED** at Scorer time (no story existed yet); closed the gap by adding a `WithBoxedHeader` story + a real Playwright screenshot before commit, confirming clean render with no overlap/left-shift | 0 |
| B1a | `zimmCountryLanguageMismatch.css.ts`: fix `root` padding to `paddingInline: 2xl (32px)` / `paddingBlock: 1200 (48px)`, replacing the placeholder uniform `xl` (24px) — confirmed via live Figma re-fetch after re-authenticating; see "Steps not in the original plan" below | *(not yet committed — pending B1's own commit)* | **PASS** (round 1) — combined Orchestrator+Scorer pass confirmed diff scoped to `root` only, gates hold (79/1187/0, audit unchanged); its one flagged caveat (does the taller padding still fit A4's mobile content-height behaviour?) resolved by a live Playwright measurement during the 2026-09-12 checkpoint — no overflow, both CTAs fully visible at 390×844 | 0 |
| A5 | `ZimmDrawer`: fix `prompt` header sizing — add `md+` override (92px auto-height, `py:24`) matching `xLarge`'s existing pattern, plus widen `HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE` 72px→80px (shared baseStyle, affects every drawer consumer) — discovered via the same checkpoint; see below | *(in progress)* | *(pending)* | — |

## Steps not in the original plan (discovered mid-build via Marcel's own review)

Two real defects surfaced from Marcel comparing the rendered B1 component against Figma and against
`zimmWishlistAuthDrawer`, neither anticipated by `plan.md`:

- **A3 — `ZimmDrawer` `boxedHeader` mode.** B1 used `labelledBy` (no title text), which only ever got
  the floating `position:absolute` close button — unlike Wishlist/Login, which get a real in-flow
  header box via `title`. `zimmDrawer.css.ts`'s own file comment groups "Regional Storefront" with
  Wishlist/Login as `Desktop Small` consumers, implying it should match their structure. Added a
  `boxedHeader?: boolean` flag to the `labelledBy` branch that renders the same real header box
  `title` gets, with an empty title span (holds the flex space, pushes the close button right, no
  visible text — the accessible name still comes from `labelledBy`). New file:
  `zimmDrawer/index.test.tsx` (first test this component has ever had). Heavy Tester: all 9 targeted
  verification points CONFIRMED, including real compiler probes proving the type system genuinely
  rejects `title` + `boxedHeader` together. One non-blocking finding: the header band and content area
  render the identical white colour (pre-existing, shared with Wishlist/Login, not new to this diff) —
  no visual separation cue beyond blank space. **Not yet committed** — needs Orchestrator + Scorer,
  then a visual checkpoint (this changes rendered output).
- **A4 — mobile height fix.** See table above. Committed as `622ddf8`.

Both of these replace an earlier, now-superseded fix: a hand-measured `CLOSE_BUTTON_CLEARANCE`
padding-hack on B1's own recipe, which papered over the missing header box rather than fixing the
structural gap. Removed as part of A3.

- **B1a — content-container padding.** Marcel spotted a padding discrepancy by eye during visual
  review; Figma access had dropped mid-session and was re-authenticated specifically to check this.
  Live `get_design_context` against the real `pdp/drawer` instance (node `40002218:52408`) returned
  `px-32px py-48px` — the shipped value was a flagged placeholder (`var(--zimm-scale-xl)`, 24px
  uniform) borrowed from `zimmAuthDrawerContent.css.ts` pending a real Figma read. Wrong in both
  magnitude and shape. Fixed to `paddingInline: 2xl / paddingBlock: 1200`. Marcel explicitly
  sequenced this ahead of a second discrepancy found in the same investigation (the header band —
  see A5 below): "make the fix for the content padding first, then let's revisit the other
  discovered discrepancy."
- **A5 — `prompt` header sizing.** A 2026-09-12 checkpoint (Marcel's explicit request, before
  starting B2 — "let's execute a design comparison between what we've built so far against the
  design specs for 831 and 689") re-verified every spacing/gap value shipped so far against fresh
  Figma fetches across all three breakpoints and both variants. Everything else held
  (content-container padding now correct at every breakpoint, `root`'s responsive 80px/64px gap,
  16px heading-to-body and button-to-button gaps, Language variant byte-identical to Location,
  402px width floor, mobile content-height + B1a's taller padding coexisting without overflow —
  live-measured, closing a caveat the B1a Scorer pass had flagged). One real gap surfaced: `prompt`
  never got its own `header` override, so it silently inherits the mobile treatment (72px,
  `paddingBlock:0`) at every breakpoint — live-measured identical at 390/834/1440px. Figma specifies
  92px auto-height (`py:24` around the 44px close-icon row) at `md+` (confirmed via two independent
  fetches, genuine Desktop Small node `40002218:52408` and Tablet node `40007204:186134`, identical
  numbers both times — one step, not two) and a fixed 80px on mobile (node `40007204:186159`), 8px
  taller than the shared `HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE` constant. Marcel chose to fix both in one pass,
  explicitly accepting that widening `HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE` touches every `ZimmDrawer` consumer
  (Wishlist, Login, Find in Boutique, Cookies, Notify Me), not just this story's own `prompt` size.

## Gates (real numbers, not claims)

| Gate | Baseline | After A1 | After A2 | After A4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | exit 0, clean | exit 0, clean | exit 0, clean | exit 0, clean |
| `npm run test` | 76 files / 1164 tests / 0 failures | 77 files / 1170 tests / 0 failures | 77 files / 1170 tests / 0 failures (unchanged, as required) | 79 files / 1187 tests / 0 failures (includes A3's uncommitted `index.test.tsx`, +8 in `zimmDrawer.css.test.ts`) |
| `npm run lint` | 870 problems (823 errors, 47 warnings) | not re-checked | not re-checked | not re-checked — recheck before final gate |
| `npm run audit:tokens` | 3 unacknowledged | 3 unacknowledged | 3 unacknowledged | 3 unacknowledged (unchanged — `'auto'`/bare `0` don't match the hex/px/rem/em regex) |

## UNIFORM findings (recur across steps, not one-offs)

- **`npm install` (Step 0) unconditionally runs the repo's `postinstall` chain** (`compile-translations && compile-translations:pseudo && generate:registry`), which dirties `.claude/registry/*.md` (expected, harmless, auto-swept by the pre-commit hook) and, once, two Tier-2-owned translation compiled JSONs unrelated to any step in this plan (reverted before A1's commit, won't recur since Step 0 only runs once). Noted so nobody re-investigates this drift as if it were new at a later step.
- **Self-reports need independent re-verification, not trust.** A1's implementer disputed one of the plan's own file:line citations (`zimmTabs/index.tsx:48`) as pointing at a nonexistent file — both the Tester and the Scorer independently checked and found the citation correct, the dispute wrong. Nothing in the shipped diff was affected, but it's a reason later steps' self-verified claims (C2's "diff is comment-only," C3's "cookie-before-navigate ordering") should be re-run by whoever scores them, not accepted as written.

## Could not verify

- **Real rendered geometry** — structurally impossible from this loop (jsdom reports every rect as 0). A1's visual checkpoint (Storybook `Elements/ZimmDrawer` → `Small` and `Prompt` stories at 390/834/1440px) was completed by Marcel directly and confirmed good before commit.

## Outstanding

- Steps B1/B2 (the component + Contentful seed) not yet started.
- Steps C1/C2/C3 (SFCC-689's helpers, `useCountryConfig` fix, `_app` mount) not yet started.
- `npm run lint` baseline count (870/823/47) should be re-checked at least once before the final gate, to confirm no step introduced new lint errors — not re-run per-step per the plan's own scale call, but the final gate requires a clean comparison.
- **`drawer.close` has no seeding path anywhere in this plan — DECIDED (Marcel, 2026-09-12): track as a standalone follow-up, do NOT fold into B2.** A2 wires the close button through `useUiCopy()`, but B2 only seeds its own 8 regional-prompt keys and `seedLoginDrawerUiCopy.mjs` seeds an unrelated namespace — so every locale renders the English `"Close"` fallback until a separate seed entry (or a fourth script) is created. Both the Orchestrator and Scorer flagged this independently when A2 closed out. Explicitly out of B2's scope by Marcel's own call — a new follow-up ticket/task should own creating the `drawer.close` Contentful entry, not this plan. Say so in the PR body: A2 wires the fix, it does not make it live in any locale yet.

consumer's mobile header height, not just this story's own `prompt` size — same one-file blast
radius as A1's width-floor change, which also widened a shared constant on the reasoning that it
could only help, never hurt, existing consumers. Re-verified twice (implementer, then
independently by the Orchestrator via a fresh grep of every real `<ZimmDrawer` render site): the
only genuinely affected real consumer is `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer` (Wishlist/Login) — Find in
Boutique and the PDP tab drawer pass neither `title` nor `boxedHeader`, so they never render
`header` at all (floating close button only); Cookies/Notify Me don't exist as built consumers
yet. The `header` override's own first draft named all five as affected — corrected once checked.

**Round 1 rework (Tester-caught defect):** the `md+` header override alone didn't reach 92px when
live-measured — 72px, unchanged. Root cause: `index.tsx`'s `title`/`boxedHeader` render branch has
always rendered the close button bare, with no explicit height, so the row's real height was the
button's own small intrinsic size, not Figma's 44px `drawer-header-options` row. `24 + 24 + 24 =
72`, coincidentally the old value. This was latent in every *other* `paddingBlock`-driven header
too (only `xLarge`, unused — Cart isn't a drawer yet) — every header override that used
`minHeight` instead papered over it, since `minHeight` forces the total box height regardless of
the button's real size. Fix: a new `headerCloseButton` recipe part (44px row, centred, no
`position:absolute` — deliberately not reusing `closeButton`, which would pull the button out of
flow and reproduce the exact bug) wired through `zimmDrawer.css.ts` + `index.tsx`, touching two
pre-existing tests whose own assertions were one DOM level too shallow after the new wrapper.
Final live measurement, independently reproduced twice (me, then the Orchestrator from scratch):
80px/0-padding @390px, 92px/24px-padding @834px and @1440px — matches Figma exactly.

**Round 2 rework (Scorer-caught gap):** no recipe-value test asserted the new
`headerCloseButton.height` or `prompt.header`'s new `md+` values — only the part's *name* was
checked. Added two tests to `zimmDrawer.css.test.ts`, each proven red before green per this file's
own established method. Final: 79 files/1189 tests/0 failures, tsc clean, audit unchanged at 3.

**Open question raised independently by both the Tester and the Scorer, not yet decided:**
`small` (the real desktop drawer for Wishlist/Login) has no `header` override at any breakpoint —
it inherits the mobile-compact treatment even at 834px/1440px. The same Figma "Desktop Small" node
(`40002218:52408`) this fix cites for `prompt` is also the node the file's own header-comment
table names for `small`. If that reading is right, Wishlist/Login's desktop headers may have the
same 72/80-vs-92px gap `prompt` just had — a pre-existing gap in shipped components, unrelated to
this diff and unverified by it. Not fixed as part of A5. Needs a decision: fix now (touches
Wishlist/Login's live rendered header height), or log as a follow-up ticket.

content.subject: A1 — ZimmDrawer prompt size + width floor

content.subject: A2 — ZimmDrawer localised close-button label

content.description: New organism: discriminated union on variant, VARIATION_CONFIG dispatch, composes ZimmDrawer size="prompt" + 2x ZimmButton. Recipe, story, test, registration in theme/components/index.ts (Tier 2). Heavy loop per plan.

content.subject: C2 — fix useCountryConfig EU site resolution
content.description: One-line fix: site?.sfccSiteId ?? site?.id. Corrected test mocks (currently mock an impossible site.id value). Comment-only correction in footer/index.tsx. Medium loop, mandatory fail-on-purpose (red-before-green) since the existing suite passed against an impossible mock for months.

content.subject: C3 — mount language prompt in _app
content.description: New zimmLanguagePrompt container + mount in _app/index.tsx (Tier 2) + _app/index.test.tsx (Tier 2, additive-only — must not touch the SFCC-863 DNT regression assertions). Heavy loop, sharpest review point in the PR. Second visual checkpoint owed after this step.

content.subject: Final gate + handoff to PostBuild
content.description: npm run build-storybook + interaction/a11y suite, npm run test:story, npm run test:max-file-size, cr review --base develop. Finalise handoff.md, present to Marcel, hand off to zimmerMANNPostBuild. Do not push, do not open a PR.

content.subject: A3 — ZimmDrawer boxedHeader mode (headerless-title)
content.description: Extend ZimmDrawer with a boxedHeader flag on the labelledBy branch: renders the real in-flow header box (matching the title path's structure) with an empty title span instead of the floating position:absolute close button. No CSS/recipe changes needed — header/headerTitle/closeButton parts already exist. Then update zimmCountryLanguageMismatch to use it, removing the CLOSE_BUTTON_CLEARANCE padding hack from A1's rework. Discovered via Marcel's design comparison against zimmWishlistAuthDrawer — zimmDrawer.css.ts's own file comment groups "Regional Storefront" with Wishlist/Login as Desktop Small consumers, all of which use the boxed title-row pattern.

content.subject: A4 — fix ZimmDrawer prompt mobile height (bottom:auto)
content.description: prompt variant's height:'auto' never actually shrunk to content on mobile — position:fixed with top/right/bottom all pinned means height:auto stretches to fill, it doesn't shrink-wrap. Proven via real Playwright measurement at 440x956: panel rendered 898px tall (viewport-58), 572px of empty space below the last button. Fix: add bottom:'auto' to prompt's base-level content styles so top:0 anchors it and height:auto can actually shrink to content. maxHeight cap stays as a safety net. Only affects prompt (every other size sets an explicit height value, never relied on auto). Must be verified with a real rendered measurement, not just a recipe-value string assertion — that's exactly what let this bug ship undetected through A1.

content.subject: B1a — fix content-container padding (32px/48px, not 24px)
content.description: zimmCountryLanguageMismatch.css.ts's root.padding is uniform 24px (var(--zimm-scale-xl)), borrowed from a different component's precedent. Confirmed via fresh get_design_context on the real wrapping content-container node (I40002218:52408;40007204:171894): actual design is paddingInline 32px (--zimm-scale-2xl) + paddingBlock 48px (--zimm-scale-1200), not a uniform value. Both map to existing tokens.

content.subject: A5 — fix ZimmDrawer prompt header sizing (92px md+, 80px mobile)
content.description: Discovered via design-comparison checkpoint before B2: prompt variant's header inherits mobile treatment (72px, 0 vertical padding) at every breakpoint instead of Figma's 92px auto-height (py:24) at md+. Also HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE itself is 72px vs Figma's 80px fixed. Marcel approved fixing both, accepting the shared-constant change affects Wishlist/Login/Find-in-Boutique/Cookies/Notify Me too. zm-implementer dispatched (agent a5e5c67f8e1e3a507).

Zimmermann PWA Kit, branch `feature/SFCC-831-689_country-language-mismatch`. This is step A6 of the SFCC-831/689 build — another mid-build fix discovered via the same design-comparison checkpoint that produced A5 (already committed as `625241f`, "fix(drawer): SFCC-831 correct ZimmDrawer header sizing to match Figma" — read that commit's diff with `git show 625241f` to see the exact pattern you're extending). Marcel has explicitly approved this scope.

## Finding (confirmed live this session)

`ZimmDrawer`'s `small` variant has no `header` override at any breakpoint — it inherits the mobile-compact `baseStyle.header` treatment (now 80px, `paddingBlock:0`, since A5) at every width including tablet/desktop. Live Playwright measurement of `commerce-zimmwishlistauthdrawer--default` (the real, only consumer of `small`'s `header` part — `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.tsx` passes `title={drawerTitle}`) confirmed: header height is **80px at 390px, 834px, AND 1440px** — identical everywhere, same shape of defect `prompt` had before A5.

Figma's `pdp/drawer` component (the shared template both `small`'s consumers and `prompt`'s consumer instantiate) showed byte-identical header chrome across 4 independent fetches this session (Location at Desktop Small/Tablet/Mobile, Language at Desktop Small): `py:24px` around a 44px row = 92px total at `md+`, 80px fixed on mobile — regardless of which content variant instantiates the component. The file's own header-comment table (top of `zimmDrawer.css.ts`) already groups `small` and `prompt` under the same Figma category, "Desktop Small." No Wishlist/Login-specific Figma frame was available to cite directly this session — Marcel explicitly approved fixing this based on the shared-component evidence rather than waiting for one.

## The fix — should be pure config, no new plumbing

A5 already built the hard part: a `headerCloseButton` recipe part (in `zimmDrawer.css.ts`'s `baseStyle`) that gives the boxed close button (rendered whenever `title` or `boxedHeader` is passed) a real 44px in-flow row — read `git show 625241f -- overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/index.tsx` to see how `index.tsx` already wires this for every consumer that renders the `header` part, including `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer`. You should NOT need to touch `index.tsx` at all this time — the plumbing is generic, not `prompt`-specific.

**In `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/zimmDrawer.css.ts`:** add a `header` key to the `small` variant (it currently only has `content`), matching `prompt.header`'s and `xLarge.header`'s existing shape exactly:
```ts
header: {
  [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
    minHeight: 'unset',
    paddingBlock: HEADER_PADDING_Y,
  },
},
```
Add a comment citing this session's finding (byte-identical header chrome across the 4 Figma fetches for `prompt`, live-confirmed 80px-everywhere defect on the real `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer` consumer, Marcel's explicit approval to proceed without a Wishlist-specific Figma citation) — match this file's existing comment density/style (see `prompt.header`'s own comment, added in A5, as the reference for tone and thoroughness).

## Test coverage — do this from the start this time

A5 needed two rework rounds, the second one purely because recipe-value tests were missing for new values. Don't repeat that here: add the equivalent test to `zimmDrawer.css.test.ts` in the same PR-round as the fix, following the exact pattern the `prompt.header` test added in A5's rework uses (search for `headerCloseButton` in that file to find it and the `stylesAboveMd` helper it uses). Prove it red against the pre-fix `small.header` (`undefined`) before confirming it green, per this file's own established method.

## Verify before reporting back

- Confirm via `git diff`/`git status` that only `zimmDrawer.css.ts` and `zimmDrawer.css.test.ts` changed — nothing else needed touching if the plumbing really is generic as claimed. If you find you DO need to touch `index.tsx`, stop and report why rather than proceeding — that would mean my understanding of A5's plumbing is wrong and needs re-checking before you continue.
- Run `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run test`, `npm run audit:tokens`. Baseline (post-A5, current HEAD): tsc clean; 79 files/1189 tests/0 failures; audit 3 unacknowledged.
- Do NOT touch `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` or `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCountryLanguageMismatch/` — those are pre-existing uncommitted B1 work, unrelated to this step.

Report back with the diff and gate numbers. The live re-verification (re-measuring `commerce-zimmwishlistauthdrawer--default` in a real browser) will happen after your report, not something you need to do yourself.

1	# Build Plan — SFCC-831 + SFCC-689
2	
3	> Produced by `zm-planner` 2026-09-12, synthesising the full decision record in
4	> `./decisions.md` and `../SFCC-689/decisions.md` (both authoritative — every decision in them
5	> was taken with Marcel in session and must not be re-litigated during the build).
6	> Original gate: `./findings.md`. Superseded 2026-09-09 run: `./findings-2026-09-09.md`.
7	>
8	> **Invoke as `zimmerMANNBuild SFCC-831`** — one branch, one PR, both stories.
9	
10	**Branch:** `feature/SFCC-831-689_country-language-mismatch` (clean, on `develop` @ `2510cea`)
11	
12	**Verified baseline, captured 2026-09-12 before any change:**
13	
14	| Gate | Baseline |
15	|---|---|
16	| `npx tsc --noEmit` | exit 0, no output |
17	| `npm run test` | **76 files / 1164 tests / 0 failures**, ~29s |
18	| `npm run audit:tokens` | **"3 unacknowledged violation(s) found."** (pre-existing, untouched by this work) |
19	| `git status` | clean |
20	
21	Every pass criterion below is written against those four numbers. They are the only honest
22	definition of "didn't break anything."
23	
24	---
25	
26	## 1. Goal statement
27	
28	Build the EU country/language mismatch prompt as prescribed by **SFCC-831** (the presentational
29	component) and **SFCC-689** (the trigger that consumes it), as designed in Figma component
30	symbols `40002103:7407` / `40002104:10184` / `40002104:10133` (location) and `40002431:38549` /
31	`:38533` / `:38575` (language), as approached by the FED handbook's co-located-recipe and
32	container/presentational rules, as established by `zimmProductCard` (discriminated-union
33	`VARIATION_CONFIG` dispatch) and `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer` (drawer composition), using a **new
34	`Zimm`-namespaced theme recipe plus a new opt-in `prompt` size on the existing shared
35	`ZimmDrawer` atom** — not a new drawer shell and not a foundation-token change. Done means: a
36	shopper on `/it-eu/` whose browser reports French sees a modal drawer, in the storefront's own
37	language, offering to switch to `/fr-eu/`; acting or dismissing writes a 7-day `zimm-region-pref`
38	cookie at `path=/` before a hard navigation; and the prompt never fires again inside that window,
39	on any EU path. Both stories ship in **one branch, one PR**, with the drawer's incidental defect
40	fixes named and attributed in the PR body.
41	
42	---
43	
44	## 2. Scale call — one branch, eight commits, and a deliberately trimmed loop
45	
46	**One branch, one PR, eight commits.** This is a single coherent feature with one reviewer
47	audience: SFCC-689 is unbuildable without SFCC-831, and SFCC-831 has no consumer without
48	SFCC-689. Splitting them creates a PR that ships dead code and a second PR that can't be reviewed
49	without the first. Marcel already decided this; the commit boundaries below are what make it
50	reviewable anyway.
51	
52	**Commit boundaries** (the `commit-msg` hook enforces conventional commits; the PR *title* stays
53	plain-conventional with no SFCC key, per the accepted-PR standard):
54	
55	| # | Subject |
56	|---|---|
57	| 0 | *(no commit — install + baseline)* |
58	| A1 | `feat(drawer): SFCC-831 add prompt size and narrow-panel width floor` |
59	| A2 | `fix(a11y): SFCC-831 localise ZimmDrawer close button label` |
60	| B1 | `feat(regional): SFCC-831 add country/language mismatch prompt component` |
61	| B2 | `chore(contentful): SFCC-831 seed regional prompt uiCopy keys` |
62	| C1 | `feat(regional): SFCC-689 add region cookie, cross-site URL and eligibility helpers` |
63	| C2 | `fix(regional): SFCC-689 match useCountryConfig on sfccSiteId` |
64	| C3 | `feat(regional): SFCC-689 show EU language prompt on first visit` |
65	
66	The A1/A2 split is not cosmetic. It is how the reviewer sees, from `git log` alone, that the
67	`prompt` size serves SFCC-831 and the close-label fix serves four unrelated consumers. That is the
68	framing a separate PR would have given, at zero process cost.
69	
70	### How much loop this actually warrants
71	
72	Full loop (implement → test → scope-check → score) on **A1, B1, C1, C3** only. These four carry
73	all the new logic, all the new test files, and the only Tier 2 mount.
74	
75	**Deliberately dropped, and why:**
76	
77	- **No `useLanguagePrompt` hook.** The container in C3 has one `useState` and one `useEffect`; all
78	  the branching lives in the already-unit-tested pure predicate. `components.md`'s
79	  extract-to-hook threshold is not met. If the container exceeds ~80 lines during implementation,
80	  extract then — do not pre-build it.
81	- **No E2E / Playwright spec, and no `.feature` file.** Two independent reasons: the gherkin-first
82	  workflow forbids writing a spec before Lead QA signs off a `.feature`, and adding a `regional`
83	  area to the change-scoped E2E allow-list means editing `.github/workflows/qa.yml`, which is
84	  **Tier 1**. Out of scope; see the closing note for the consequence.
85	- **No `npm run test:max-file-size` per step.** It runs a full production build.
86	  `ZimmDrawer`/`ZimmButton`/`ZimmIcon` are already in the `_app` chunk via header and footer, so
87	  the marginal bundle cost is near zero. Run it once at the end only if the Test-tier gate
88	  complains.
89	- **No copy-first step anywhere.** Confirmed: every file touched is either an existing Zimmermann
90	  override (`zimmDrawer`, `_app`, `footer`, `theme/components/index.ts`) or Zimmermann-authored
91	  from scratch. Nothing mirrors an un-overridden path under
92	  `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`. **The builder must not pause for copy-first.**
93	- **Light loop on A2, B2, C2** — two-line change, a standalone script, and a one-line fix
94	  respectively.

# Build Plan — SFCC-831 + SFCC-689

> Produced by `zm-planner` 2026-09-12, synthesising the full decision record in
> `./decisions.md` and `../SFCC-689/decisions.md` (both authoritative — every decision in them
> was taken with Marcel in session and must not be re-litigated during the build).
> Original gate: `./findings.md`. Superseded 2026-09-09 run: `./findings-2026-09-09.md`.
>
> **Invoke as `zimmerMANNBuild SFCC-831`** — one branch, one PR, both stories.

**Branch:** `feature/SFCC-831-689_country-language-mismatch` (clean, on `develop` @ `2510cea`)

**Verified baseline, captured 2026-09-12 before any change:**

| Gate | Baseline |
|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | exit 0, no output |
| `npm run test` | **76 files / 1164 tests / 0 failures**, ~29s |
| `npm run audit:tokens` | **"3 unacknowledged violation(s) found."** (pre-existing, untouched by this work) |
| `git status` | clean |

Every pass criterion below is written against those four numbers. They are the only honest
definition of "didn't break anything."

---

## 1. Goal statement

Build the EU country/language mismatch prompt as prescribed by **SFCC-831** (the presentational
component) and **SFCC-689** (the trigger that consumes it), as designed in Figma component
symbols `40002103:7407` / `40002104:10184` / `40002104:10133` (location) and `40002431:38549` /
`:38533` / `:38575` (language), as approached by the FED handbook's co-located-recipe and
container/presentational rules, as established by `zimmProductCard` (discriminated-union
`VARIATION_CONFIG` dispatch) and `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer` (drawer composition), using a **new
`Zimm`-namespaced theme recipe plus a new opt-in `prompt` size on the existing shared
`ZimmDrawer` atom** — not a new drawer shell and not a foundation-token change. Done means: a
shopper on `/it-eu/` whose browser reports French sees a modal drawer, in the storefront's own
language, offering to switch to `/fr-eu/`; acting or dismissing writes a 7-day `zimm-region-pref`
cookie at `path=/` before a hard navigation; and the prompt never fires again inside that window,
on any EU path. Both stories ship in **one branch, one PR**, with the drawer's incidental defect
fixes named and attributed in the PR body.

---

## 2. Scale call — one branch, eight commits, and a deliberately trimmed loop

**One branch, one PR, eight commits.** This is a single coherent feature with one reviewer
audience: SFCC-689 is unbuildable without SFCC-831, and SFCC-831 has no consumer without
SFCC-689. Splitting them creates a PR that ships dead code and a second PR that can't be reviewed
without the first. Marcel already decided this; the commit boundaries below are what make it
reviewable anyway.

**Commit boundaries** (the `commit-msg` hook enforces conventional commits; the PR *title* stays
plain-conventional with no SFCC key, per the accepted-PR standard):

| # | Subject |
|---|---|
| 0 | *(no commit — install + baseline)* |
| A1 | `feat(drawer): SFCC-831 add prompt size and narrow-panel width floor` |
| A2 | `fix(a11y): SFCC-831 localise ZimmDrawer close button label` |
| B1 | `feat(regional): SFCC-831 add country/language mismatch prompt component` |
| B2 | `chore(contentful): SFCC-831 seed regional prompt uiCopy keys` |
| C1 | `feat(regional): SFCC-689 add region cookie, cross-site URL and eligibility helpers` |
| C2 | `fix(regional): SFCC-689 match useCountryConfig on sfccSiteId` |
| C3 | `feat(regional): SFCC-689 show EU language prompt on first visit` |

The A1/A2 split is not cosmetic. It is how the reviewer sees, from `git log` alone, that the
`prompt` size serves SFCC-831 and the close-label fix serves four unrelated consumers. That is the
framing a separate PR would have given, at zero process cost.

### How much loop this actually warrants

Full loop (implement → test → scope-check → score) on **A1, B1, C1, C3** only. These four carry
all the new logic, all the new test files, and the only Tier 2 mount.

**Deliberately dropped, and why:**

- **No `useLanguagePrompt` hook.** The container in C3 has one `useState` and one `useEffect`; all
  the branching lives in the already-unit-tested pure predicate. `components.md`'s
  extract-to-hook threshold is not met. If the container exceeds ~80 lines during implementation,
  extract then — do not pre-build it.
- **No E2E / Playwright spec, and no `.feature` file.** Two independent reasons: the gherkin-first
  workflow forbids writing a spec before Lead QA signs off a `.feature`, and adding a `regional`
  area to the change-scoped E2E allow-list means editing `.github/workflows/qa.yml`, which is
  **Tier 1**. Out of scope; see the closing note for the consequence.
- **No `npm run test:max-file-size` per step.** It runs a full production build.
  `ZimmDrawer`/`ZimmButton`/`ZimmIcon` are already in the `_app` chunk via header and footer, so
  the marginal bundle cost is near zero. Run it once at the end only if the Test-tier gate
  complains.
- **No copy-first step anywhere.** Confirmed: every file touched is either an existing Zimmermann
  override (`zimmDrawer`, `_app`, `footer`, `theme/components/index.ts`) or Zimmermann-authored
  from scratch. Nothing mirrors an un-overridden path under
  `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`. **The builder must not pause for copy-first.**
- **Light loop on A2, B2, C2** — two-line change, a standalone script, and a one-line fix
  respectively.

---

## 3. File manifest

Tiers taken **only** from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`, `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` and
`/CODEOWNERS`. `.claude/registry/*.md` was not consulted.

### Tier 2 — gated

| File | Op | Why Tier 2 | Owners |
|---|---|---|---|
| `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` | MODIFY | `protectedFiles.md` → Theme Component Styles; CODEOWNERS:117 | tier-2-approvers, tier-1-approvers |
| `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx` | MODIFY | `protectedFiles.md` → Global Shell; CODEOWNERS:91 | squad-a, squad-b, tier-2, tier-1 |
| `overrides/app/components/_app/index.test.tsx` | MODIFY | **same directory rule** — CODEOWNERS:91 matches the whole `_app/` folder | squad-a, squad-b, tier-2, tier-1 |
| `overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx` | MODIFY *(comment-only)* | `protectedFiles.md` → Global Shell; CODEOWNERS:87 | squad-a, squad-b, tier-2, tier-1 |

> **FLAGGED — there are four Tier 2 files, not the three previously expected.** The fourth is
> `_app/index.test.tsx`.
>
> **Consequence:** if the builder assumes three, it will hit a red suite it wasn't expecting and
> may "fix" it by weakening the SFCC-863 assertions — the exact regression that suite exists to
> prevent.
>
> **Mechanism:** `ZimmButton` imports `ZimmIcon` at `ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/index.tsx:3`, and
> `ZimmIcon` pulls the base SFCC icons barrel whose top-level `AmexSymbol.viewBox = …` side effect
> throws under Vitest **at module-evaluation time**, not at render. So the moment `_app/index.tsx`
> statically imports anything that reaches `ZimmDrawer`, `_app/index.test.tsx` throws on import —
> before a single assertion runs.
>
> **Fix:** one `vi.mock` of the new container in `_app/index.test.tsx`, plus one new positive
> assertion (see step C3). Same directory, same owners, no new approver required. Say so in the PR
> body so the reviewer doesn't read a test-file edit next to a DNT regression suite as tampering.

### Tier 3 — squad-owned, no approval gate

All route to `@ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-a @ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-b` via CODEOWNERS:176
(`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/`) or :186 (`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts`).

| File | Op | Phase |
|---|---|---|
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/zimmDrawer.css.ts` | MODIFY | A1 |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/index.tsx` | MODIFY | A1 + A2 |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/index.stories.tsx` | MODIFY | A1 |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/zimmDrawer.css.test.ts` | **ADD** | A1 |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.test.tsx` | MODIFY *(comment-only, line 9)* | A2 |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCountryLanguageMismatch/index.tsx` | **ADD** | B1 |
| `…/zimmCountryLanguageMismatch/zimmCountryLanguageMismatch.css.ts` | **ADD** | B1 |
| `…/zimmCountryLanguageMismatch/index.stories.tsx` | **ADD** | B1 |
| `…/zimmCountryLanguageMismatch/index.test.tsx` | **ADD** | B1 |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmLanguagePrompt/index.tsx` | **ADD** | C3 |
| `…/zimmLanguagePrompt/index.stories.tsx` | **ADD** | C3 |
| `…/zimmLanguagePrompt/index.test.tsx` | **ADD** | C3 |

### Tier 4 — unowned by CODEOWNERS, no gate

| File | Op | Phase |
|---|---|---|
| `overrides/app/utils/regionPrefCookie.ts` + `.test.ts` | **ADD** | C1 |
| `overrides/app/utils/crossSiteUrl.ts` + `.test.ts` | **ADD** | C1 |
| `overrides/app/utils/shouldShowLanguagePrompt.ts` + `.test.ts` | **ADD** | C1 |
| `overrides/app/hooks/useCountryConfig.ts` | MODIFY | C2 |
| `overrides/app/hooks/useCountryConfig.test.ts` | MODIFY | C2 |
| `scripts/contentful/seedRegionalPromptUiCopy.mjs` | **ADD** | B2 |

**Confirmed untiered, not inferred:** `overrides/app/utils/` and
`overrides/app/hooks/useCountryConfig.ts` match no CODEOWNERS rule (the hook rules name individual
kebab-case files only). `scripts/contentful/` root is unmatched — only `buildTemplate.js`,
`setup/installTemplate.mjs` and `content-types/` are gated.

### BLOCKED — must not be touched

`package.json` (Tier 1, CODEOWNERS:53). **Do not add an npm script for the seed.** The precedent
`scripts/contentful/seedLoginDrawerUiCopy.mjs` has none and is run by hand; adding one converts a
Tier 4 change into a Tier 1 one for no benefit.

Also out of scope, unchanged: `config/` (Tier 1, absolute — no verified-session exception),
`overrides/app/config/countries.ts` (Tier 1), `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` (Tier 1),
`.github/workflows/qa.yml` (Tier 1).

---

## 4. Sequenced steps

### Step 0 — install and baseline *(no commit)*

The SFCC-662 Adyen merge changed `package.json` and ~1,564 lockfile lines, and this branch was cut
after it.

- Run `npm install`.
- **Pass criteria:** `npm install` exits 0; `node -e "require.resolve('@adyen/adyen-salesforce-pwa/package.json')"` resolves; `git status --porcelain` is still clean (install must not dirty the lockfile).
- **Note:** evidence suggests this is already satisfied — `node_modules/.package-lock.json` is dated within a minute of `package-lock.json` and the Adyen package resolves. Run it anyway; a no-op costs seconds.
- **Loop:** implement only. No test, no score.

---

### Step A1 — `ZimmDrawer`: `prompt` size + narrow-panel width floor

**Changes**

1. `zimmDrawer.css.ts`: add `PANEL_MIN_NARROW = '25.125rem'` (402px). It **must** carry a comment
   containing `provisional`, `pending`, `placeholder`, or `audit-allow:` — `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs:59`
   matches on exactly that vocabulary, case-insensitive. Follow the existing `audit-allow:` comment
   at `zimmDrawer.css.ts:54`.
2. Add a shared `NARROW_WIDTH_ABOVE_MD` object, same technique as the existing `INSET_COMPACT`, so

### Step C1 — three pure helpers *(no dependency on A or B — parallelisable)*

**Changes** — all in `overrides/app/utils/`:

**`regionPrefCookie.ts`** — contract, spec only what's specified:

```
zimm-region-pref=1|l=<epochSeconds>|c=<epochSeconds>
path=/; samesite=lax; secure; max-age=<long>
```

`l` = language prompt dismissed/acted, `c` = country prompt. **No `s` flag** — nothing specifies
storing a manual selection; the `1|` version prefix means adding one later strands nothing. Exports
a named `LANGUAGE_PROMPT_SUPPRESSION_DAYS = 7` constant. **Parse and serialise must be pure and
isomorphic** (zero `document` reference), with thin client `get`/`set` on top — the client writes it
and the server will later read it from the `Cookie` header in `request-processor.js`. One module,
four eventual consumers (689, 823, 688, 817); otherwise 817 re-implements the parser and the two
drift. `try/catch` on **read and write** (Safari private mode throws on *read* — see
`useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts:30`), plus an SSR guard (`typeof document === 'undefined'`). Not
`httpOnly`.

**`crossSiteUrl.ts`** — strip the base path and the current site alias, then
`buildUrl(path, targetAlias, targetLocale)`. `getPathWithLocale` cannot be reused: it swaps the
locale *within one site*, and the four EU languages are separate **sites**. Preserve the path, drop
`refine` (`disallowParams: ['refine']`), matching `footer/index.jsx:152`. Returns a string; the
caller performs the hard navigation.

**`shouldShowLanguagePrompt.ts`** — pure predicate:

```ts
shouldShowLanguagePrompt({ sfccSiteId, currentLanguage, browserLanguages, suppressedAt, now })
  : { show: boolean; targetLanguage?: string }
```

naturally excluding EU International (`ZimmermannEUIntl`, English-only). **Match on the primary
subtag, both sides**: browsers report `fr-FR`, `it-CH`, `en-AU`; our site locales are `fr`, `it`,
`es`, `en-GB`. `fr-FR`→`fr` and our `en-GB`→`en`, or a French shopper reporting `fr-FR` never
matches and the prompt silently never fires. Read-time window enforcement, not browser expiry.

content.subject: A3 — ZimmDrawer boxedHeader mode (headerless-title)
content.description: Extend ZimmDrawer with a boxedHeader flag on the labelledBy branch: renders the real in-flow header box (matching the title path's structure) with an empty title span instead of the floating position:absolute close button. No CSS/recipe changes needed — header/headerTitle/closeButton parts already exist. Then update zimmCountryLanguageMismatch to use it, removing the CLOSE_BUTTON_CLEARANCE padding hack from A1's rework. Discovered via Marcel's design comparison against zimmWishlistAuthDrawer — zimmDrawer.css.ts's own file comment groups "Regional Storefront" with Wishlist/Login as Desktop Small consumers, all of which use the boxed title-row pattern.

content.subject: A4 — fix ZimmDrawer prompt mobile height (bottom:auto)
content.description: prompt variant's height:'auto' never actually shrunk to content on mobile — position:fixed with top/right/bottom all pinned means height:auto stretches to fill, it doesn't shrink-wrap. Proven via real Playwright measurement at 440x956: panel rendered 898px tall (viewport-58), 572px of empty space below the last button. Fix: add bottom:'auto' to prompt's base-level content styles so top:0 anchors it and height:auto can actually shrink to content. maxHeight cap stays as a safety net. Only affects prompt (every other size sets an explicit height value, never relied on auto). Must be verified with a real rendered measurement, not just a recipe-value string assertion — that's exactly what let this bug ship undetected through A1.

content.subject: B1a — fix content-container padding (32px/48px, not 24px)
content.description: zimmCountryLanguageMismatch.css.ts's root.padding is uniform 24px (var(--zimm-scale-xl)), borrowed from a different component's precedent. Confirmed via fresh get_design_context on the real wrapping content-container node (I40002218:52408;40007204:171894): actual design is paddingInline 32px (--zimm-scale-2xl) + paddingBlock 48px (--zimm-scale-1200), not a uniform value. Both map to existing tokens.

content.subject: A5 — fix ZimmDrawer prompt header sizing (92px md+, 80px mobile)
content.description: Discovered via design-comparison checkpoint before B2: prompt variant's header inherits mobile treatment (72px, 0 vertical padding) at every breakpoint instead of Figma's 92px auto-height (py:24) at md+. Also HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE itself is 72px vs Figma's 80px fixed. Marcel approved fixing both, accepting the shared-constant change affects Wishlist/Login/Find-in-Boutique/Cookies/Notify Me too. zm-implementer dispatched (agent a5e5c67f8e1e3a507).

content.subject: A6 — fix ZimmDrawer small header sizing (92px md+, matches Wishlist/Login)
content.description: Confirmed live: ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer (small variant) renders header at 80px at every breakpoint including tablet/desktop, same shape of bug prompt had before A5. small has no header override at md+ at all. Fix: add the same header override prompt got in A5 (minHeight:'unset', paddingBlock: HEADER_PADDING_Y at md+) — headerCloseButton plumbing already exists from A5, so this should be pure config. Marcel approved fixing now based on shared pdp/drawer component evidence (4-for-4 identical header chrome across Location/Language at every breakpoint), no Wishlist-specific Figma frame available.

content.text:
Here are the 8 `uiCopy` keys and their English values, grouped by variant — exactly as seeded in `scripts/contentful/seedRegionalPromptUiCopy.mjs` and byte-matched against the component's own fallbacks:

**Location variant** (country mismatch)
| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| `regional.locationPrompt.heading` | Looks like you're {inCountry} |
| `regional.locationPrompt.body` | You're currently shopping on {currentStore}. Switch to {targetStore} for local pricing, currency and shipping options. |
| `regional.locationPrompt.cta.switch` | Switch to {targetStore} |
| `regional.locationPrompt.cta.stay` | Stay on {currentStore} |

**Language variant** (EU language mismatch)
| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| `regional.languagePrompt.heading` | Welcome to Zimmermann Europe |
| `regional.languagePrompt.body` | Welcome to Zimmermann Europe. We noticed you're {inCountry}, would you like to view our site {inLanguage}? |
| `regional.languagePrompt.cta.switch` | View {inLanguage} |
| `regional.languagePrompt.cta.stay` | Continue {inCurrentLanguage} |

Two things worth knowing when a copy author looks at these: every `{token}` is a full phrase, not a bare noun — `{inCountry}` already includes its preposition (e.g. "in Germany," not just "Germany"), and `{inLanguage}`/`{inCurrentLanguage}` likewise (e.g. "in French"). That's deliberate — French, Italian, and Spanish inflect prepositions, so a bare `{country}` slot can't be made grammatical in translation. And store sentence case, not caps — `textStyle="heading3"` and the buttons both uppercase via CSS already, so a capitalised fallback would double-transform.

Yes and no, depending on where you look — worth being precise here:

**Yes — this is exactly what's coded right now.** These are the literal fallback strings in `ZimmCountryLanguageMismatch/index.tsx`'s `VARIATION_CONFIG` (committed as `a89b8b3`), and I byte-compared them against the seed script's values directly — all 8 match exactly, zero drift. If you open Storybook right now (`Layout/ZimmCountryLanguageMismatch` → `Location`/`Language`), this is precisely the text you'll see, because that's the only place this component renders today.

**No — not live anywhere else yet, and not in Contentful yet.** Two things haven't happened:
- **No consumer exists in the real app.** This component isn't mounted anywhere on the actual storefront — that's C3's job (mounting it in `_app`), which hasn't been built. Visit any EU domestic page right now and you won't see this drawer at all, regardless of your browser language.
- **Contentful has nothing seeded.** The seed script exists but, per what I flagged earlier, nobody has run it against any environment yet. `useUiCopy`'s `t(key, fallback, values)` call is what's carrying these strings today — it degrades to the inline `fallback` argument whenever Contentful has no matching entry (or isn't reachable). So even once C3 mounts the component, it would keep showing exactly this English text via the code fallback until the seed script actually runs — Contentful only starts overriding it, per-locale, after that.

So: code and Storybook agree today; the real app and Contentful are both still pending later steps.

2	
3	export type UiCopyContextValue = {
4	  /**
5	   * Returns the CMS value for `key`, or `fallback` while the fetch is loading, on fetch
6	   * error, or when no `uiCopy` entry with that key exists yet. When `values` is passed,
7	   * every `{token}` in the resolved string (CMS value or fallback) is replaced from it —
8	   * mirrors react-intl's `formatMessage(descriptor, values)` shape closely enough that a
9	   * call site converting away from react-intl only has to change the function, not the
10	   * string template itself.
11	   */
12	  t: (key: string, fallback: string, values?: Record<string, string | number>) => string;
13	  isLoading: boolean;
14	};
15	
16	/**
17	 * Replaces every `{token}` in `template` with `values[token]`, left untouched if `token`
18	 * isn't in `values`. Shared by both the real UiCopyProvider and FALLBACK_ONLY below so a
19	 * key with no matching Contentful entry still interpolates correctly against its fallback.
20	 */
21	export const interpolateUiCopy = (template: string, values?: Record<string, string | number>): string => {
22	  if (!values) return template;
23	  return template.replace(/\{(\w+)\}/g, (match, token: string) => (token in values ? String(values[token]) : match));
24	};
25	
26	/**
27	 * Populated by UiCopyProvider (overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider), mounted once in
28	 * _app-config. Not meant to be consumed directly — call useUiCopy() instead, which supplies
29	 * the no-Provider fallback.
30	 */
31	export const UiCopyContext = createContext<UiCopyContextValue | undefined>(undefined);
32	
33	const FALLBACK_ONLY: UiCopyContextValue = {
34	  t: (_key: string, fallback: string, values?: Record<string, string | number>) => interpolateUiCopy(fallback, values),
35	  isLoading: false,
36	};
37	
38	/**
39	 * App-wide UI-copy lookup, backed by Contentful's uiCopy content type — one entry per string,
40	 * fetched in a single bulk call by UiCopyProvider and shared via context, the same pattern
41	 * this app already uses for translations (`useIntl`) rather than the per-page container-fetch
42	 * pattern commerce-sdk-react hooks use. uiCopy is app-wide static content, not page-specific
43	 * business data, so it's safe to call from any component — including presentational leaves —
44	 * without threading it through as a prop.
45	 *
46	 * Safe to call with no UiCopyProvider mounted above it (Storybook, an isolated unit test):
47	 * degrades to fallback-only text instead of throwing, so every call site stays functional and
48	 * testable with zero setup.
49	 *
50	 * @returns `t` lookup function plus `isLoading`
51	 */
52	export const useUiCopy = (): UiCopyContextValue => useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY;

content.text:
Traced the actual code path — here's exactly how it works, end to end.

**The content model.** `uiCopy` has 4 fields: `key` (the lookup id, e.g. `regional.locationPrompt.heading` — not localized, must be unique), `value` (the actual string — **the only localized field**), `title` and `description` (both editor/translator-facing only, never rendered). So one Contentful entry can hold a different `value` per locale, all under the same `key`.

**The fetch.** `UiCopyProvider` is mounted once, high up in `_app-config` — so it runs once per page load, not once per component. It does a single bulk call: `GET cdn.contentful.com/.../entries?content_type=uiCopy&locale=<current-site-locale>` — every `uiCopy` entry in the space, already resolved to the current site's locale by Contentful itself, in one request. This is a **plain client-side `fetch` in a `useEffect`**, not a build-time bake — no SSG, no React Query cache layer. That matters for your question specifically: **a Contentful edit goes live on the next real page load, no redeploy needed.**

**The lookup.** The response gets folded into an in-memory `Map<key, value>`. The `t(key, fallback, values)` function every component calls does `copyMap.get(key) ?? fallback` — Contentful's value wins if the key exists for that locale, otherwise it drops to the hardcoded fallback string in the component's own code. Either way, `{token}` placeholders get interpolated from `values` afterward, so `{inCountry}` etc. work the same regardless of which string won.

**Applied to what you just seeded:**

1. Right after running the seed script (English only, on whatever environment you target), every EU locale — `fr`, `it`, `es`, `en-GB` — will render the **English** text. Not because the app is falling back to its own code anymore, but because Contentful's own locale config (`optional: true, fallbackCode: 'en'`) serves English when a locale-specific value doesn't exist yet, transparently, before the response even reaches the app. Visually identical to today's Storybook fallback, but now sourced from the CMS.
2. The moment a content editor authors the French value for, say, `regional.languagePrompt.heading` in Contentful Studio and publishes it, the **very next page load** on `/fr-eu/` pulls that French string instead — Contentful now has a real `fr` value for that key, so no fallback is needed. Zero code change, zero deploy.
3. If Contentful is unreachable or misconfigured, `error` gets set, `copyMap` stays empty, and every `t()` call quietly drops to the component's own hardcoded fallback — a Contentful outage degrades to English everywhere rather than breaking the drawer, matching this project's "fail independently" rule.

One gap this exposes concretely: until C3 mounts `ZimmCountryLanguageMismatch` somewhere under `_app`, none of this fires at all — `UiCopyProvider` only feeds components that are actually rendered, and today this component only renders in Storybook (no Provider there, so it always shows the raw code fallback regardless of Contentful's state).

1	# 02 — Contentful (CMS)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Contentful is the headless CMS for editorial content: homepage modules, promotional banners, lookbooks, campaign landing pages, size guide fallback content (primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay — PRD-053), footer, and editorial blocks on PLPs and PDPs. The storefront reads published content via the **Delivery API (CDA)** from both SSR and the browser, reads draft content via the **Preview API (CPA)** in editor sessions, and receives **publish webhooks** to clear the SSR cache.
6	
7	In scope:
8	
9	- Reading published content via the Delivery API
10	- Reading draft content via the Preview API in editor preview sessions
11	- Live preview in Contentful Studio
12	- Locale-specific content via Contentful's native localisation
13	- Contentful Studio Experiences — drag-and-drop page composition by editors
14	- Receiving publish webhooks to clear stale SSR cache entries
15	
16	Out of scope of this document:
17	
18	- Content type schema sync (managed in code via the Management API — see §2)
19	- Asset uploads and content editing in Contentful Studio
20	- Webhooks from Contentful to SFCC (none planned)
21	
22	**Content ownership.** SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001). Rows marked *pending* are unconfirmed (see §11).
23	
24	| Surface | SFCC owns | Contentful owns | Status |
25	|---|---|---|---|
26	| Homepage | Commerce data for embedded product refs | All modules — hero, banners, campaign blocks | Confirmed |
27	| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
28	| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
29	| Size guides | — | Fallback content only — primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay (PRD-053, confirmed 2026-06-19); Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product | Updated |
30	| Footer | — | All content | Confirmed |
31	| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | *Whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful is pending* |
32	| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary size guide is Measmerize — PRD-053) | *Which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer is pending* |
33	| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | *Pending* |
34	| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy — managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005); clickable badges link to category/PLP. Contentful is not the source of badge content unless explicitly confirmed. | — | Confirmed |
35	
36	## 2. Content type management (build-time)
37	
38	Content type schemas are managed in code, not in the Contentful UI:
39	
40	- Schema definitions live in the PWA repo and are reviewed via pull request.
41	- A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
42	- Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time.
43	
44	## 3. Browser-side architecture
45	
46	```
47	PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
48	        │
49	        ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
50	        │        SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
51	        │        post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
52	        │
53	        ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
54	        │        Editor preview only. Token set in MRT as an env var
55	        │        on dev/test/sit/uat only (never staging or prod).
56	        │        Reached client-side on the /preview route and via
57	        │        ?preview on Experience pages — both are gated: if no
58	        │        CPA token is present, both paths fail explicitly with
59	        │        a 404 and are noindex (no delivery fallback). The Live
60	        │        Preview SDK requires the token in the browser for
61	        │        postMessage-based real-time updates.
62	        │
63	        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
64	        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
65	        │
66	        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
67	                 Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
68	                 HMAC-verified with a shared secret.
69	```
70	
71	- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
72	- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
73	- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the `/preview` route renders the entry inside Studio's iframe. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK subscribes to `postMessage` events from Studio for real-time content updates. The CPA token is used client-side here — this is required by the SDK and is acceptable because: (a) the token is set only on dev/test/sit/uat (never staging or prod) MRT environments, (b) the route returns a 404 when no preview token is present, and (c) the route is `noindex`. The MRT proxy approach was considered but deferred in favour of the simpler client-side SDK integration.
74	- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.
75	
76	## 4. Authentication and credentials
77	
78	| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
79	|---|---|---|
80	| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
81	| Preview API token (CPA) | `/preview` route and `?preview` on Experience pages (dev/test/sit/uat only — never staging or prod) | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. Set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only; never set on staging or prod. Both the `/preview` route and `?preview` Experience pages return 404 and are `noindex` when the token is absent — they fail explicitly, with no delivery fallback. Used client-side by the Live Preview SDK (required for postMessage updates). |
82	| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
83	| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |
84	
85	Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.
86	
87	## 5. Data exchanged
88	
89	| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
90	|---|---|---|
91	| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
92	| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
93	| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
94	| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
95	| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |
96	
97	No PII flows through Contentful.
98	
99	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
100	
101	- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
102	- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
103	- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
104	- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
105	- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
106	- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.
107	
108	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
109	
110	- A single Contentful Space serves all eight storefronts via Contentful's native locale model.
111	- The active locale is resolved from the URL prefix and passed as `locale=` on every CDA request. Eleven active locales: en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE.
112	- Region-specific entries (banners, promotions, editorial that varies by site) are filtered at query time using the active SFCC site ID.
113	
114	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
115	
116	| Failure | Behaviour |
117	|---|---|
118	| Contentful CDA unavailable | Page renders without editorial content. Editorial slots show empty; commerce data is never blocked on a CMS read. |
119	| Stale cached content after a publish | Tolerated within the 60-second TTL. The publish webhook normally clears affected entries in seconds; the TTL is the safety net if the webhook drops. |
120	| Preview API returns broken or unpublished refs | Editor preview only — render a placeholder. Production traffic never hits this path. |
121	| Asset (image) 404 | Show alt text and a graceful placeholder. |
122	| 429 rate limit on CDA | Exponential backoff and retry. The SSR cache makes this rare in practice. |
123	| Publish webhook fails HMAC verification | Reject and log. Storefront continues serving from cache; the TTL picks up the change. |
124	| Live preview iframe disconnects | Storefront silently returns to non-preview mode. |
125	
126	## 9. Security and privacy
127	
128	- The CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment. Embedding in the bundle is safe per Contentful's published guidance.
129	- The CPA token is set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only — never on staging or prod. It reaches the browser on the `/preview` route and `?preview` Experience pages, both of which return 404 when no token is present. Both preview paths are `noindex` and not linked from any storefront navigation. This is a deliberate tradeoff: the Live Preview SDK requires the token client-side for real-time postMessage updates, and the non-prod-only gate means the token is never in a production bundle.
130	- The CMA token is held only on the CI host — never embedded, never in PR diffs.
131	- No PII is handled by Contentful.
132	
133	## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation
134	
135	1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all eight storefronts.
136	2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC owns all commerce data, Contentful owns editorial. Not yet confirmed is the split on composed pages: which editorial blocks appear on PDP and PLP, whether they are authored in SFCC Page Designer or Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or built in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu includes Contentful-authored promotional tiles. The working assumption is in the ownership table in §1.
137	3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provide per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be tested against a real Contentful environment.
138
