| Size guides | — | Fallback content only — primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay (PRD-053, confirmed 2026-06-19); Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product | Updated |
| Footer | — | All content | Confirmed |
| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | *Whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful is pending* |
| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary size guide is Measmerize — PRD-053) | *Which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer is pending* |
| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | *Pending* |
| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy — managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005); clickable badges link to category/PLP. Contentful is not the source of badge content unless explicitly confirmed. | — | Confirmed |

## 2. Content type management (build-time)

Content type schemas are managed in code, not in the Contentful UI:

- Schema definitions live in the PWA repo and are reviewed via pull request.
- A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
- Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time.

## 3. Browser-side architecture

```
PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
        │
        ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
        │        SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
        │        post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
        │
        ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
        │        Editor preview only. Token set in MRT as an env var
        │        on dev/test/sit/uat only (never staging or prod).
        │        Reached client-side on the /preview route and via
        │        ?preview on Experience pages — both are gated: if no
        │        CPA token is present, both paths fail explicitly with
        │        a 404 and are noindex (no delivery fallback). The Live
        │        Preview SDK requires the token in the browser for
        │        postMessage-based real-time updates.
        │
        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
        │
        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
                 Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
                 HMAC-verified with a shared secret.
```

- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the `/preview` route renders the entry inside Studio's iframe. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK subscribes to `postMessage` events from Studio for real-time content updates. The CPA token is used client-side here — this is required by the SDK and is acceptable because: (a) the token is set only on dev/test/sit/uat (never staging or prod) MRT environments, (b) the route returns a 404 when no preview token is present, and (c) the route is `noindex`. The MRT proxy approach was considered but deferred in favour of the simpler client-side SDK integration.
- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.

## 4. Authentication and credentials

| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
|---|---|---|
| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
| Preview API token (CPA) | `/preview` route and `?preview` on Experience pages (dev/test/sit/uat only — never staging or prod) | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. Set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only; never set on staging or prod. Both the `/preview` route and `?preview` Experience pages return 404 and are `noindex` when the token is absent — they fail explicitly, with no delivery fallback. Used client-side by the Live Preview SDK (required for postMessage updates). |
| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |

Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.

## 5. Data exchanged

| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |

No PII flows through Contentful.

## 6. Performance and loading strategy

- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.

## 7. Multi-region behaviour

- A single Contentful Space serves all eight storefronts via Contentful's native locale model.
- The active locale is resolved from the URL prefix and passed as `locale=` on every CDA request. Eleven active locales: en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE.
- Region-specific entries (banners, promotions, editorial that varies by site) are filtered at query time using the active SFCC site ID.

## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Contentful CDA unavailable | Page renders without editorial content. Editorial slots show empty; commerce data is never blocked on a CMS read. |
| Stale cached content after a publish | Tolerated within the 60-second TTL. The publish webhook normally clears affected entries in seconds; the TTL is the safety net if the webhook drops. |
| Preview API returns broken or unpublished refs | Editor preview only — render a placeholder. Production traffic never hits this path. |
| Asset (image) 404 | Show alt text and a graceful placeholder. |
| 429 rate limit on CDA | Exponential backoff and retry. The SSR cache makes this rare in practice. |
| Publish webhook fails HMAC verification | Reject and log. Storefront continues serving from cache; the TTL picks up the change. |
| Live preview iframe disconnects | Storefront silently returns to non-preview mode. |

## 9. Security and privacy

- The CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment. Embedding in the bundle is safe per Contentful's published guidance.
- The CPA token is set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only — never on staging or prod. It reaches the browser on the `/preview` route and `?preview` Experience pages, both of which return 404 when no token is present. Both preview paths are `noindex` and not linked from any storefront navigation. This is a deliberate tradeoff: the Live Preview SDK requires the token client-side for real-time postMessage updates, and the non-prod-only gate means the token is never in a production bundle.
- The CMA token is held only on the CI host — never embedded, never in PR diffs.
- No PII is handled by Contentful.

## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation

1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all eight storefronts.
2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC owns all commerce data, Contentful owns editorial. Not yet confirmed is the split on composed pages: which editorial blocks appear on PDP and PLP, whether they are authored in SFCC Page Designer or Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or built in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu includes Contentful-authored promotional tiles. The working assumption is in the ownership table in §1.
3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provide per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be tested against a real Contentful environment.

lastPrompt: where does transperfect come into play?

content.text:
TransPerfect sits **entirely outside the PWA's boundary** — I checked `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md`, `.docs/prd/regional.md`, and `.docs/memory/projectState.md` to confirm this rather than guess, since I hadn't verified the actual mechanism before.

**What the docs actually say:** there was originally a ticket (**REG-047**) for a formal, end-to-end, PWA-aware Contentful↔TransPerfect↔SFCC translation pipeline. It was **de-scoped** (2026-05-25). What replaced it: *"Translation occurs directly between Contentful and Transperfect outside the PWA Kit's concern"* — confirmed in three separate docs, all saying the same thing: *"Contentful ↔ Transperfect directly... Out-of-band... No PWA involvement."*

So concretely:
- The PWA **never talks to TransPerfect**. No API call, no webhook, no trigger — that integration is owned by Contentful and the vendor directly, addressed (per `.docs/integration/index.md`) by the separate SFCC↔MuleSoft middleware design, not this repo.
- The **exact trigger mechanism is still an open question in this project's own docs** — literally marked `TBD` in `architecture.md` ("Translation workflow trigger TBD") and `projectState.md` ("Translation trigger workflow with TransPerfect (TBD)"). Nobody's nailed down yet whether that's a scheduled export, a Contentful Connect app, or a manual step a content editor kicks off.
- The PWA's job starts and ends at **being a consumer**: whatever locale value TransPerfect's translation eventually lands in Contentful's `value` field, `UiCopyProvider` picks it up on the next fetch, exactly as I described earlier — same mechanism, doesn't care how the value got there.

**The one place TransPerfect actually shapes what I built:** the `description` field on every `uiCopy` entry. The content type's own comment explains why it exists: *"Translators working key-by-key in Transperfect can't see the string in situ on the page."* Whatever the handoff mechanism turns out to be, it apparently doesn't give the translator a screenshot of the actual drawer — just the key and the string. That's exactly why I wrote the 8 descriptions the way I did (explaining what `{inCountry}` means, that it already carries its own preposition, which button is primary vs. secondary) — that context is the only thing standing between a translator and a guess.

One more distinction the PRD draws, for completeness: this only covers Contentful-held copy. SFCC-held strings (system messages, validation copy) go through a separate path entirely — static JSON files — which doesn't apply to this component at all since every one of its 8 strings lives in Contentful.

content.text:
**TransPerfect translates it — a content editor doesn't hand-type the French.** The docs are explicit that translators work "key-by-key" at TransPerfect, which is the language service vendor's actual job, not something a Contentful editor does themselves. So the flow is:

1. English `value.en` gets authored in Contentful — that's what the seed script just did for these 8 keys.
2. TransPerfect takes that English source and produces the French (and Italian, Spanish) translation.
3. The translated text gets written back into Contentful's `fr`/`it`/`es` locale fields for the same entries.
4. Once published, that's verbatim what `UiCopyProvider` fetches and what shows up in the drawer — the app never transforms or re-derives anything, it just reads whatever string sits in the locale field it asked for.

So yes — whatever TransPerfect produces from the English source is exactly what a French shopper sees. The `description` field is there precisely because that translator never sees the drawer itself, only the key/value/description in isolation.

**The part worth flagging plainly:** seeding these 8 English entries does **not** by itself guarantee French/Italian/Spanish translations will appear. The mechanism that gets a *new* Contentful entry in front of a TransPerfect translator in the first place is the piece this project's own docs mark as unresolved — `architecture.md` and `projectState.md` both say the trigger workflow is still `TBD`. So after this seed script runs, these 8 keys will sit in Contentful as English-only (correctly falling back to English on every locale, not broken) until whoever owns the TransPerfect relationship actually gets them into that translation queue — that's a process step outside this build, and outside the PWA's visibility entirely. Worth confirming with whoever runs that relationship (Emma Kirwan's name comes up as an open-item owner elsewhere in `decisions.md`) that new `uiCopy` keys like these actually get picked up, rather than assuming seeding alone is sufficient.

content.text:
Mostly yes for the ongoing translation work itself, but not a clean "nothing else" — there are three real gaps worth being precise about, because assuming "seed and done" could let something silently break for a real shopper.

**What genuinely is TransPerfect's / Contentful's, not ours:**
- Producing the French/Italian/Spanish text itself.
- The vendor-side sync that moves translated values back into Contentful.

**What's still ours (or at least, still nobody's until someone claims it):**

1. **Actually running the seed script.** Writing it isn't the same as it having executed against a real environment. This is still open — nobody's confirmed it authenticates, creates all 8 entries correctly, or that a second run is genuinely idempotent. That's on us (or whoever holds the Contentful token).

2. **Keeping the English source in sync going forward.** The seed script's own header comment says this explicitly: if the component's hardcoded fallback ever changes (a copy tweak, a bug fix to the wording), someone has to update *both* `index.tsx`'s fallback *and* Contentful's English value, or they silently drift apart. Nothing enforces that after today — it's a standing discipline, not a one-time task.

3. **Making sure these 8 keys actually reach a translator at all.** This is the one I flagged last turn and it's worth repeating plainly: the trigger that gets a *new* Contentful key into TransPerfect's queue is marked `TBD` in this project's own architecture docs. Seeding English does not automatically mean French is coming — it just means French will correctly *fall back* to English until someone outside this build's scope (whoever owns the TransPerfect relationship — Emma Kirwan's name is attached to a related open item in `decisions.md`) makes sure translation actually gets requested.

**One more thing genuinely worth a spot-check once translations do land, that isn't clearly anyone's stated job today:** nothing in this pipeline validates that a translator preserves the `{token}` syntax correctly. The interpolation regex (`\{(\w+)\}`) is strict — no spaces, no translated token names. If TransPerfect's French output renders `{inCountry}` as `{ inCountry }` or translates "inCountry" into something else, the substitution silently fails and a real shopper sees the literal `{inCountry}` text in the drawer instead of their country name. Reordering the token within the sentence is fine and expected (that's the whole reason the tokens carry full phrases); mangling the token itself isn't, and nothing catches it automatically. Worth a manual look at the French/Italian/Spanish output once it exists, not something to assume is fine because the English version tested clean.

So: seeding is the whole of *our code's* job, but not the whole of *making French correctly appear in the drawer* — that still has an unrun step, a maintenance obligation, and one unowned handoff sitting between here and there.

content.text:
Pulled directly from `config/sites.overlay.js` — the authoritative routing source. "EU" actually splits into two genuinely separate groups, which matters because SFCC-689's own trigger logic only targets one of them:

**EU Domestic** — 4 separate PWA sites, single-locale each, all backed by the **same** real SFCC site (`ZimmermannEU`) — this is the group SFCC-689's language mismatch prompt actually targets:

| PWA site ID | SFCC site ID | Locale | URL slug |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ZimmermannEUen` | `ZimmermannEU` | `en-GB` | `/en-eu/` |
| `ZimmermannEUfr` | `ZimmermannEU` | `fr` | `/fr-eu/` |
| `ZimmermannEUit` | `ZimmermannEU` | `it` | `/it-eu/` |
| `ZimmermannEUes` | `ZimmermannEU` | `es` | `/es-eu/` |

**EU International** — a separate storefront entirely, **not** part of the four above:

| PWA site ID | SFCC site ID | Locale | URL slug |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ZimmermannEUIntl` | *(none — own SFCC site)* | `en-CH` | `/en-ch/` |

EU International is English-only, uses Global-e checkout (covers non-EU Europe, Africa, and rest-of-world), and is explicitly excluded from this build's language-mismatch logic — `shouldShowLanguagePrompt`'s gate is `sfccSiteId === 'ZimmermannEU'`, which naturally never matches `ZimmermannEUIntl` since it has no `sfccSiteId` override at all (its PWA `id` and SFCC id are the same).

One nuance worth keeping straight, since it's the exact bug C2 fixes: the four EU Domestic PWA sites each have their **own** `id` (`ZimmermannEUfr`, etc.) but share **one** underlying `sfccSiteId` (`ZimmermannEU`). Anything matching against `site.id` directly will never see "EU domestic" as a group — it has to check `sfccSiteId`, which only the four EU domestic entries even define.

content.text: This is very revealing. Let me confirm one more piece — which Contentful API the live app actually uses (published-only Delivery API, vs. draft-inclusive Preview API) — to close the loop definitively.

Found it — this is a **Contentful data gap, not primarily a code bug**, though there's one misleading comment worth fixing too. Confirmed by directly querying the live `dev` environment (the one my local `.env` is configured against).

## Root cause

`FooterContainer` fetches via the **Delivery API only** (`useContentfulClient()` with no `preview` flag → published content only). That's the load-bearing fact here.

**What actually exists in Contentful (`dev` environment) right now:**

- **11 `region` entries total.** The 4 covering EU Domestic — `ZimmermannEUen`, `ZimmermannEUfr`, `ZimmermannEUit`, `ZimmermannEUes` — are all sitting as **unpublished drafts**. Every other region (AU, US, USIntl, UK, HK, ME, **EUIntl**) is published.
- **Only 1 published `footerConfig` entry exists** — "Footer Config — Australia (placeholder hrefs)" — and its `regions` array explicitly lists exactly 7 sites: `AU, ME, HK, EUIntl, UK, USIntl, US`. The 4 EU Domestic sites are not in it.
- There's a second footerConfig entry titled "Footer Config — Europe" — but it's **also unpublished**, and oddly its own `regions` list is identical to the Australia one (AU/ME/HK/EUIntl/UK/USIntl/US) — it doesn't reference the 4 EU-domestic regions either, published or not.
- **No unscoped/global footerConfig entry exists** (one with `regions` omitted, which the schema's own comment says should act as the catch-all default). Both entries that exist are region-scoped, so there's no fallback to catch a site that matches nothing.

**Why en-ch works and the other four don't:** `ZimmermannEUIntl` (en-ch) is directly named in the one published footerConfig's `regions` list, so it matches and renders. `ZimmermannEUen/fr/it/es` are absent from every published footerConfig's `regions` list — and even if they weren't, their own `region` entries aren't published yet either — so `pickMostSpecificByRegion` finds nothing eligible, `footerData` stays `null`, and per the container's own `if (!footerData) return null`, the *entire* footer (columns, subscribe section, logo band, bottom bar — everything) disappears. That matches exactly what you're seeing.

## On the code side

`footer/index.tsx` itself isn't the bug here — I checked whether this was the same `sfccSiteId`-vs-`id` mismatch as `useCountryConfig` (C2), and it isn't: the region content model already has one `region` entry *per PWA site* (a separate entry for `ZimmermannEUfr` etc., not one shared `ZimmermannEU`), so matching directly on `site.id` is actually the correct design here, not a bug.

There **is** a misleading comment, though — `footer/index.tsx:194-196` says this `site.id` lookup is *"confirmed against `useCountryConfig.ts`'s identical client-side pattern... the existing precedent for this exact lookup"* — citing a hook we already know is buggy (that's C2) as if it were verified-correct prior art. It happens not to share the actual defect, but the citation is bad practice regardless. This is already anticipated in this build's own plan (C2's file manifest names this exact comment for a reword, comment-only, no logic change) — so it's already queued, just not done yet.

## Caveat

I only queried the `dev` environment (what my local `.env` points at) — Contentful content is authored and published independently per environment, so `test`/`sit`/`staging`/`uat`/`prod` could each be in a different state. If what you observed was on a different tier, worth re-running this same check there before assuming the fix is identical.

## What this needs (not done — investigation only, as asked)

Two Contentful publish actions, no code required: publish the 4 EU-domestic `region` entries, and either add them to an existing footerConfig's `regions` list or create a proper EU-domestic-scoped one (and publish it) — or add a genuine unscoped/global footerConfig entry as the missing fallback the schema was designed to have. That's a content action for whoever owns Contentful editing, not an engineering fix.

content.text:
Yes — one very concrete, directly transferable finding, and one reassuring confirmation.

**The transferable lesson: "exists in Contentful" and "live to a shopper" are two different states, gated by publish status — and that gate applies per-write, not just per-entry.** The footer bug wasn't that the EU region data didn't exist — it existed, it just was never published, so the Delivery API (what the live app actually reads) silently skipped it. The same mechanic applies to what happens *next* for our 8 keys: when TransPerfect's French/Italian/Spanish translations get written back into Contentful, adding a new locale value to an *already-published* entry doesn't automatically go live — Contentful tracks that as a published entry with pending changes, and the Delivery API keeps serving the old (English) version until someone explicitly publishes again. So there are actually **two separate points of failure** standing between "seeded" and "a French shopper sees French," not one:

1. Does anyone tell TransPerfect to translate these keys at all (the trigger-mechanism gap, still `TBD` per the architecture docs — already flagged).
2. **Once translated, does whatever writes the French value back into Contentful also re-publish the entry** — or does it silently sit as an unpublished change, invisible via CDA, exactly like the footer's EU regions are right now.

Neither of these is something our code controls — but it's now a concrete thing to verify with whoever owns the Contentful↔TransPerfect side, worded precisely instead of a vague "make sure it works": *does the translation write-back also publish, or does someone need to click publish manually per entry per locale?*

**The reassuring part:** our own seed script doesn't have the footer's problem. Every entry it creates is immediately followed by `client.entry.publish(...)` in the same script run — the English baseline goes live the moment the script succeeds, unlike whatever process left the footer's EU regions sitting as drafts. That risk exists at the *next* write (the translation one), not at ours.

**One more thing this comparison confirms, architecturally:** footer uses a heavier content model — a `region` entity plus a `regions` reference array, because footer content can genuinely differ *by storefront identity* (different contact links per market), not just by language. Our drawer's copy doesn't have that shape — every token (`{inCountry}`, `{targetStore}`, etc.) is injected per-shopper at render time from props, not from a separate Contentful entry per country. So `uiCopy`'s flat, native-localization model (one entry, one `value` field, localized directly by Contentful's own locale system) is the right fit, not an oversimplification — we don't need footer's region-reference indirection, and that indirection is exactly what introduced the join-key mismatch risk the footer's data is currently exposed to. Our locale key (`fr`, `it`, `es`) is already the same identifier `config/sites.overlay.js` defines per PWA site directly — no intermediate reference entry to misalign in the first place.

The whole lookup mechanism (`copyMap.get(key)`) only works because of this — if translations arrived as separate new entries, there'd be no way to tie a French entry back to the same `key` an English one uses.

**Not the frontend, confirmed.** Our code never translates anything, ever. It only ever asks Contentful "give me the value for this key, in this locale" and displays whatever comes back. The project's own docs are explicit about this: *"No FE work required beyond consuming the translated Contentful payloads."* Zero translation logic lives in our repo or runs in the browser.

**Now the honest part — "publish, then what happens" is where I have to be careful not to make something up.** This project's own architecture docs describe the handoff as *"Contentful ↔ Transperfect directly... out-of-band... no PWA involvement"* — and then explicitly flag the actual trigger mechanism as `TBD`, twice, in two separate docs. So I can't tell you the exact button someone presses or the exact system that fires. What I *can* tell you, as general context (not confirmed for this project specifically, just how this kind of integration normally works): TransPerfect is a real, known translation vendor that offers a direct Contentful connector — the typical shape is that a connector watches specified content, ships the English source out to TransPerfect's own platform where their translators work on it, then writes the finished translation back into the same Contentful entry's locale field. That's the plausible mechanism, not a documented fact.

**Why "TBD" actually matters here, tied back to last turn's point:** that same unconfirmed step is exactly where the publish-gate risk lives. Some Contentful-LSP connectors auto-publish the moment a translation syncs back; others leave it as a draft for a human to review and publish manually. Nobody's confirmed which behavior this project's setup has — which is the concrete question worth putting to whoever owns the TransPerfect relationship, not something I should guess at.

## File 1 — `overrides/app/utils/regionPrefCookie.ts` + `.test.ts`

Cookie contract (exact, from the plan): `zimm-region-pref=1|l=<epochSeconds>|c=<epochSeconds>`, attributes `path=/; samesite=lax; secure; max-age=<long>`. `l` = language prompt dismissed/acted timestamp, `c` = country prompt dismissed/acted timestamp. No `s` flag — don't add one speculatively. Export a named `LANGUAGE_PROMPT_SUPPRESSION_DAYS = 7` constant.

Split into two halves:
- **Pure half** (parse/serialise): zero `document` reference anywhere — this is what makes it reusable server-side later (a future `request-processor.js` read from the `Cookie` header, not built now, but don't foreclose it). Unknown/garbage input must return a safe empty state, never throw.
- **Thin client half** (`get`/`set`): the only place touching `document.cookie`. `document.cookie`'s getter can throw in Safari private browsing (a real, well-documented WebKit behavior — no in-repo citation needed, just wrap it), and the setter can throw too — `try/catch` on **both** read and write, each surviving by returning/no-op'ing safely, never propagating. Guard both with `typeof document === 'undefined'` for SSR (this file may be imported by code that also runs server-side even though today's only caller is client-only — the isomorphic purity is the point, per the plan).

Tests: round-trip parse/serialise; garbage/unknown value → safe empty state, not a throw; a `document.cookie` getter that throws is survived on read; a setter that throws is survived on write; serialised string contains `path=/`, `samesite=lax`, `secure`. Every test file in this step needs each assertion proven to fail first against a deliberately wrong implementation, then pass — this file's own test conventions elsewhere in the repo (e.g. `zimmDrawer.css.test.ts`) already do this; match that rigor.

## File 2 — `overrides/app/utils/crossSiteUrl.ts` + `.test.ts`

**Why `getPathWithLocale` can't be reused — verified precisely, not just asserted:** I read `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url.js:118-156`. `getPathWithLocale(shortCode, buildUrl, opts)` resolves `site = getSiteByReference(siteRef)` from the *current* URL's site reference, then `locale = getLocaleByReference(site, shortCode)` — that second call is scoped to the *same* `site` object. There is no parameter anywhere in the function to specify a *different* target site. It can only ever swap locale within whatever site the shopper is already on. Our four EU-domestic PWA sites (`ZimmermannEUfr`/`it`/`es`/`en`) are separate sites sharing one region, so switching "language" for us really means switching site — exactly what this function structurally cannot do.

**The real `buildUrl` lives in React Context, not a plain export — this shapes your function signature.** I traced it: `useMultiSite()` (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-multi-site.js:14-23`) does `const {buildUrl: originalFn} = useContext(MultiSiteContext)` — the actual site-URL-construction logic is injected via `MultiSiteProvider`, not importable as a standalone function. This is exactly why `getPathWithLocale` itself takes `buildUrl` as its *second parameter* rather than importing it (`url.js:118`) — it's designed be called from inside a component that already has the real `buildUrl` from `useMultiSite()`, and stays hook-free itself. Follow the identical technique: `crossSiteUrl.ts`'s exported function must accept the real `buildUrl` as a parameter from its caller (which will be C3's container, a real component with `useMultiSite()` access) — it must NOT import `useMultiSite` or any hook itself, that would break "pure utility, no hook imports" and wouldn't even work outside a component tree.

**What IS safe to import directly** (plain functions, no React/hooks, confirmed via `url.js`'s own import list and `site-utils.js`): `getRouterBasePath` (from `@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk/ssr/universal/utils`), `removeBasePathFromPath`, `getParamsFromPath`, `getSiteByReference` (all three from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/site-utils.js`). Model your own path/search stripping on `getPathWithLocale`'s own logic (`url.js:118-140`: strip base path, strip current `siteRef`/`localeRef` from both pathname and search, trim a trailing `&`) — reuse those exact helpers rather than reimplementing string manipulation by hand. Verify `getSiteByReference`'s own signature yourself (read it in `site-utils.js`) to confirm it resolves by *alias* correctly, not just by real site ID — our target is always passed as an alias (e.g. `'fr-eu'`).

Suggested signature (adjust if your own reading of the above disagrees, but justify why in your report): `crossSiteUrl(path: string, targetAlias: string, targetLocale: string, buildUrl: (path: string, siteRef?: string, localeRef?: string) => string, opts?: { location?: Pick<Location, 'pathname' | 'search'>; disallowParams?: string[] }): string`. The injectable `opts.location` (mirroring `getPathWithLocale`'s own escape hatch) is what keeps this testable without a real browser `window.location`. Default `disallowParams` to `['refine']` — SFCC's own PLP search-refinement query param — since a refinement filter set on one storefront's PLP is meaningless carried into a different site's URL; this default can be overridden by a caller, not hardcoded unconditionally.

Tests: path preserved across a site switch; `refine` dropped by default, other query params kept; base path and current site alias both stripped from the input location before building the new URL; root path (`/`) handled without producing a malformed double-slash or empty string.

## File 3 — `overrides/app/utils/shouldShowLanguagePrompt.ts` + `.test.ts`

Pure predicate, signature from the plan: `shouldShowLanguagePrompt({ sfccSiteId, currentLanguage, browserLanguages, suppressedAt, now }): { show: boolean; targetLanguage?: string }`.

- Gate: `sfccSiteId === 'ZimmermannEU'` — one comparison, covers all four EU domestic sites (they share this one SFCC site ID — confirmed in `config/sites.overlay.js`), naturally excludes EU International (`ZimmermannEUIntl`, its own separate SFCC site, English-only).
- **Match on the primary subtag, both sides.** Browsers report full tags (`fr-FR`, `it-CH`, `en-AU`); our site locales are bare (`fr`, `it`, `es`, `en-GB` — confirmed in `config/sites.overlay.js`). `fr-FR` → primary subtag `fr`; our own `en-GB` → primary subtag `en`. Get this wrong and a French shopper reporting `fr-FR` never matches anything.
- Read-time window enforcement: `suppressedAt` + `LANGUAGE_PROMPT_SUPPRESSION_DAYS` (import from `regionPrefCookie.ts`, don't redefine it) vs `now`, not a cookie-native expiry.

Plus the two primary-subtag cases explicitly (`fr-FR`→`fr` matches, `en-GB`→`en` matches) — these two are the ones that would pass trivially against a stub that only checks exact string equality, so make sure your fail-on-purpose inversion actually exercises the subtag-splitting logic, not just the branch outcome.

- `npm run test` → 0 failures, file count up by 6 from current HEAD's count (confirm the exact current baseline yourself via `npm run test` before starting — don't assume a stale number).

- `git diff --stat package.json package-lock.json` → empty.
- Pure functions: no side effects, no imports from `overrides/app/hooks/` anywhere in these three files (utilities don't depend on hooks — the dependency runs the other way).
- Mandatory: for each test file, invert at least two assertions, confirm the suite goes red, revert, confirm green again. Report each red-then-green pair explicitly — don't just assert you did it.

Report back with the diff (all 6 files), the gate numbers, and the six red-then-green pairs (two per file minimum). If anything in my corrected technical detail above turns out to be wrong once you're actually reading the real source, stop and say so rather than silently working around it.

content.description: SFCC-831 plan Step A1: new `prompt` size + `minWidth` floor on `small`. Implementer → Tester → Orchestrator → Scorer all ran, PASS round 1, visual checkpoint confirmed by Marcel. Committed as e539920.

content.subject: A2 — ZimmDrawer localised close-button label
content.description: Replace hardcoded label="Close" with useUiCopy()'s t('drawer.close', 'Close'). Plus comment-only fix in zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.test.tsx:9. Light loop per plan.

content.subject: B1 — ZimmCountryLanguageMismatch component
content.description: New organism: discriminated union on variant, VARIATION_CONFIG dispatch, composes ZimmDrawer size="prompt" + 2x ZimmButton. Recipe, story, test, registration in theme/components/index.ts (Tier 2). Heavy loop per plan.

content.subject: B2 — Contentful seed script
content.description: scripts/contentful/seedRegionalPromptUiCopy.mjs — 8 keys, English values + descriptions, modelled on seedLoginDrawerUiCopy.mjs. Light loop.

content.subject: C1 — cookie, cross-site URL, and eligibility helpers
content.description: Three pure functions in overrides/app/utils/: regionPrefCookie.ts, crossSiteUrl.ts, shouldShowLanguagePrompt.ts, each with a .test.ts. No dependency on A/B. Heavy loop per plan.

content.subject: C2 — fix useCountryConfig EU site resolution
content.description: One-line fix: site?.sfccSiteId ?? site?.id. Corrected test mocks (currently mock an impossible site.id value). Comment-only correction in footer/index.tsx. Medium loop, mandatory fail-on-purpose (red-before-green) since the existing suite passed against an impossible mock for months.

content.subject: C3 — mount language prompt in _app
content.description: New zimmLanguagePrompt container + mount in _app/index.tsx (Tier 2) + _app/index.test.tsx (Tier 2, additive-only — must not touch the SFCC-863 DNT regression assertions). Heavy loop, sharpest review point in the PR. Second visual checkpoint owed after this step.

content.subject: Final gate + handoff to PostBuild
content.description: npm run build-storybook + interaction/a11y suite, npm run test:story, npm run test:max-file-size, cr review --base develop. Finalise handoff.md, present to Marcel, hand off to zimmerMANNPostBuild. Do not push, do not open a PR.

content.subject: A3 — ZimmDrawer boxedHeader mode (headerless-title)
content.description: Extend ZimmDrawer with a boxedHeader flag on the labelledBy branch: renders the real in-flow header box (matching the title path's structure) with an empty title span instead of the floating position:absolute close button. No CSS/recipe changes needed — header/headerTitle/closeButton parts already exist. Then update zimmCountryLanguageMismatch to use it, removing the CLOSE_BUTTON_CLEARANCE padding hack from A1's rework. Discovered via Marcel's design comparison against zimmWishlistAuthDrawer — zimmDrawer.css.ts's own file comment groups "Regional Storefront" with Wishlist/Login as Desktop Small consumers, all of which use the boxed title-row pattern.

content.subject: A4 — fix ZimmDrawer prompt mobile height (bottom:auto)
content.description: prompt variant's height:'auto' never actually shrunk to content on mobile — position:fixed with top/right/bottom all pinned means height:auto stretches to fill, it doesn't shrink-wrap. Proven via real Playwright measurement at 440x956: panel rendered 898px tall (viewport-58), 572px of empty space below the last button. Fix: add bottom:'auto' to prompt's base-level content styles so top:0 anchors it and height:auto can actually shrink to content. maxHeight cap stays as a safety net. Only affects prompt (every other size sets an explicit height value, never relied on auto). Must be verified with a real rendered measurement, not just a recipe-value string assertion — that's exactly what let this bug ship undetected through A1.

content.subject: B1a — fix content-container padding (32px/48px, not 24px)
content.description: zimmCountryLanguageMismatch.css.ts's root.padding is uniform 24px (var(--zimm-scale-xl)), borrowed from a different component's precedent. Confirmed via fresh get_design_context on the real wrapping content-container node (I40002218:52408;40007204:171894): actual design is paddingInline 32px (--zimm-scale-2xl) + paddingBlock 48px (--zimm-scale-1200), not a uniform value. Both map to existing tokens.

content.subject: A5 — fix ZimmDrawer prompt header sizing (92px md+, 80px mobile)
content.description: Discovered via design-comparison checkpoint before B2: prompt variant's header inherits mobile treatment (72px, 0 vertical padding) at every breakpoint instead of Figma's 92px auto-height (py:24) at md+. Also HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE itself is 72px vs Figma's 80px fixed. Marcel approved fixing both, accepting the shared-constant change affects Wishlist/Login/Find-in-Boutique/Cookies/Notify Me too. zm-implementer dispatched (agent a5e5c67f8e1e3a507).

content.subject: A6 — fix ZimmDrawer small header sizing (92px md+, matches Wishlist/Login)
content.description: Confirmed live: ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer (small variant) renders header at 80px at every breakpoint including tablet/desktop, same shape of bug prompt had before A5. small has no header override at md+ at all. Fix: add the same header override prompt got in A5 (minHeight:'unset', paddingBlock: HEADER_PADDING_Y at md+) — headerCloseButton plumbing already exists from A5, so this should be pure config. Marcel approved fixing now based on shared pdp/drawer component evidence (4-for-4 identical header chrome across Location/Language at every breakpoint), no Wishlist-specific Figma frame available.

## Step C1 — two of the plan's own citations corrected before build (2026-09-14)

Verified directly against the codebase before briefing the implementer, since both turned out not to
hold: `useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts:30` (cited for the Safari-private-mode try/catch pattern) doesn't
exist anywhere in this repo or the base `@salesforce/retail-react-app` package — grepped exhaustively,
zero hits. `footer/index.jsx:152`'s `disallowParams: ['refine']` also doesn't exist in our footer
(read the whole file; it's also `.tsx` not `.jsx`, itself a staleness signal) — the real precedent for
`disallowParams` is the *base vendor's* `getPathWithLocale` function accepting it as an `opts` field
(`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url.js:118-141`), not a Zimmermann override at
all. Implementer built `crossSiteUrl.ts` with its own accurate, self-contained rationale rather than
citing either false reference — confirmed via grep, zero mentions of "footer" or the phantom hook in
the shipped files.

**Real, verified reason `getPathWithLocale` can't be reused** (more precise than the plan's own
framing): it resolves `site = getSiteByReference(siteRef)` from the *current* URL, then scopes the
locale lookup to that same `site` object — there is no parameter to specify a *different* target
site. Confirmed by reading the function in full. `crossSiteUrl.ts`'s signature ended up
`(targetAlias, targetLocale, buildUrl, opts?)` — 4 args, not the originally-suggested 5 — dropping a
redundant `path` argument once it was confirmed `getPathWithLocale` itself never takes one either
(always reads `opts.location`). **This is the call shape C3 needs to use.**

**PASS, 1 rework round.** Heavy Tester independently re-derived the file/test-count delta via a real
`git stash` before/after (not trusting the implementer's claimed baseline), mutation-tested every
try/catch guard and `crossSiteUrl`'s param-filtering (all load-bearing), and — the most valuable
find — wrote an extra `it-CH` test case against `shouldShowLanguagePrompt.ts` and proved a narrow,
hardcoded-looking stub implementation would have passed the original 11-test suite's own mutation
testing but failed against that one additional case. One confirmed defect: a test named "...still
counts as suppressed..." whose assertion proved the opposite (window lapsed, prompt shows) — logic
and arithmetic were already correct, only the name was wrong. Fixed in a 1-line rework, re-verified.

**Open, non-blocking, distinct from REG-030:** `shouldShowLanguagePrompt.ts` only reads
`browserLanguages[0]` (the browser's single top-preference language) — never falls through to a
second preference if the first isn't one of the four supported EU languages. Documented as a
deliberate scope decision in the file's own comment, not a hidden defect, but genuinely
unconfirmed with product — a shopper whose *first* preference is German but *second* is French
currently never gets the prompt. Worth a decision before this reaches real multilingual shoppers.

**Forward-looking flag for whoever builds SFCC-823/688/817:** `regionPrefCookie.ts`'s cookie
`max-age` is 400 days (a sensible finite ceiling for the *language* prompt's 7-day window — neither
the plan nor Marcel specified a number, this was the implementer's own reasonable choice, documented
in a permanent code comment). SFCC-823's own REG-019 requirement wants the *country* prompt's
suppression to be indefinite, not time-boxed — if SFCC-823 writes its own timestamp into this same
cookie's `c` field without revisiting `max-age`, a shopper who dismissed the country prompt "forever"
would quietly get asked again after ~13 months. The `1|` version prefix is the safe extension point
if the wire format needs to change for that story, or for SFCC-817's still-unresolved "saved manual
selection" AC.

**C1 — PASS, ready to commit.** Ledgers updated. Summary:

- Three new pure utilities (`regionPrefCookie`, `crossSiteUrl`, `shouldShowLanguagePrompt`), 38 new tests, gates at 82/1228/0.
- One real defect caught and fixed: a test's name asserted the opposite of what its logic actually verified — arithmetic was correct, only the label was wrong.

- No visual checkpoint needed — pure logic files, nothing rendered.

Two things worth your attention, both non-blocking:
1. **Open product question**: `shouldShowLanguagePrompt` only checks a shopper's *first*-preference browser language. A shopper whose top preference is German but second is French never gets the prompt today. Distinct from the already-tracked REG-030 item — worth a product decision before real traffic hits this.

content.subject: A3 — ZimmDrawer boxedHeader mode (headerless-title)
content.description: Extend ZimmDrawer with a boxedHeader flag on the labelledBy branch: renders the real in-flow header box (matching the title path's structure) with an empty title span instead of the floating position:absolute close button. No CSS/recipe changes needed — header/headerTitle/closeButton parts already exist. Then update zimmCountryLanguageMismatch to use it, removing the CLOSE_BUTTON_CLEARANCE padding hack from A1's rework. Discovered via Marcel's design comparison against zimmWishlistAuthDrawer — zimmDrawer.css.ts's own file comment groups "Regional Storefront" with Wishlist/Login as Desktop Small consumers, all of which use the boxed title-row pattern.

content.subject: A4 — fix ZimmDrawer prompt mobile height (bottom:auto)
content.description: prompt variant's height:'auto' never actually shrunk to content on mobile — position:fixed with top/right/bottom all pinned means height:auto stretches to fill, it doesn't shrink-wrap. Proven via real Playwright measurement at 440x956: panel rendered 898px tall (viewport-58), 572px of empty space below the last button. Fix: add bottom:'auto' to prompt's base-level content styles so top:0 anchors it and height:auto can actually shrink to content. maxHeight cap stays as a safety net. Only affects prompt (every other size sets an explicit height value, never relied on auto). Must be verified with a real rendered measurement, not just a recipe-value string assertion — that's exactly what let this bug ship undetected through A1.

content.subject: B1a — fix content-container padding (32px/48px, not 24px)
content.description: zimmCountryLanguageMismatch.css.ts's root.padding is uniform 24px (var(--zimm-scale-xl)), borrowed from a different component's precedent. Confirmed via fresh get_design_context on the real wrapping content-container node (I40002218:52408;40007204:171894): actual design is paddingInline 32px (--zimm-scale-2xl) + paddingBlock 48px (--zimm-scale-1200), not a uniform value. Both map to existing tokens.

content.subject: A5 — fix ZimmDrawer prompt header sizing (92px md+, 80px mobile)
content.description: Discovered via design-comparison checkpoint before B2: prompt variant's header inherits mobile treatment (72px, 0 vertical padding) at every breakpoint instead of Figma's 92px auto-height (py:24) at md+. Also HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE itself is 72px vs Figma's 80px fixed. Marcel approved fixing both, accepting the shared-constant change affects Wishlist/Login/Find-in-Boutique/Cookies/Notify Me too. zm-implementer dispatched (agent a5e5c67f8e1e3a507).

content.subject: A6 — fix ZimmDrawer small header sizing (92px md+, matches Wishlist/Login)
content.description: Confirmed live: ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer (small variant) renders header at 80px at every breakpoint including tablet/desktop, same shape of bug prompt had before A5. small has no header override at md+ at all. Fix: add the same header override prompt got in A5 (minHeight:'unset', paddingBlock: HEADER_PADDING_Y at md+) — headerCloseButton plumbing already exists from A5, so this should be pure config. Marcel approved fixing now based on shared pdp/drawer component evidence (4-for-4 identical header chrome across Location/Language at every breakpoint), no Wishlist-specific Figma frame available.

content.content:
1	/**
2	 * Zimmermann country configuration — combines SCAPI-derived site/locale/
3	 * currency truth (countries.generated.ts, regenerate via
4	 * `npm run sync:regional-config`) with a hand-maintained overlay for the
5	 * fields Business Manager/SCAPI has no concept of: shipping country,
6	 * checkout ownership, and boutique region grouping.
7	 *
8	 * Used by: URL routing, IP-detection prompt, checkout redirect logic,
9	 * boutique location filtering, hreflang generation.
10	 *
11	 * When adding a country:
12	 *   1. Add it to config/sites.overlay.js (and e2e/fixtures/site.overlay.js
13	 *      if it needs e2e coverage), then run `npm run sync:regional-config`.
14	 *   2. Add its business-logic overlay entry below (shippingCountry,
15	 *      checkoutOwner, globalEPricing, boutiqueRegion).
16	 *   3. Ensure a compiled translation exists in overrides/app/static/translations/compiled/.
17	 *
18	 * Unresolved — do not hard-code:
19	 *   - NZ/Oceania currency routing
20	 *   - Denmark routing
21	 *   - China
22	 */
23	
24	import { GENERATED_COUNTRIES } from './countries.generated';
25	
26	/**
27	 * Who owns checkout for this site's domestic path.
28	 * For HK and ME, Global-e always owns checkout AND pricing from PDP onward.
29	 * For AU, US, GB, EU: SFCC owns domestic paths; Global-e takes over when the
30	 * user's shipping destination is outside the site's domestic market.
31	 */
32	export type CheckoutOwner = 'sfcc' | 'global-e' | 'hybrid';
33	
34	export type CountryConfig = {
35	  /** URL path segment, e.g. 'au', 'us', 'fr-eu' */
36	  urlSlug: string;
37	  /** The real SFCC site this locale routes to */
38	  sfccSiteId: string;
39	  /** IETF locale used by PWA Kit / SFCC, e.g. 'en-AU' */
40	  locale: string;
41	  /** ISO 4217 currency code */
42	  currency: string;
43	  /** ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 shipping/tax country */
44	  shippingCountry: string;
45	  /**
46	   * Checkout owner for this site's domestic path.
47	   * Branch checkout AND pricing logic from this field at PDP/cart level —
48	   * not only at the checkout page.
49	   */
50	  checkoutOwner: CheckoutOwner;
51	  /**
52	   * When true, Global-e owns pricing, currency, and tax display from PDP
53	   * onward — do not render SFCC prices on these paths.
54	   */
55	  globalEPricing: boolean;
56	  /** Key used to filter boutique locations for this region */
57	  boutiqueRegion: string;
58	};
59	
60	type CountryOverlayEntry = Pick<
61	  CountryConfig,
62	  'shippingCountry' | 'checkoutOwner' | 'globalEPricing' | 'boutiqueRegion'
63	>;
64	
65	/**
66	 * Hand-maintained business/geo data, keyed the same way as
67	 * countries.generated.ts (URL slug; 'au' for the root/default site).
68	 *
69	 * 'en-ca' (US international) is defined here ready to go, but has no
70	 * matching entry in countries.generated.ts yet — it's excluded from the
71	 * final COUNTRIES export below until the ZimmermannUSIntl site is added to
72	 * config/sites.overlay.js (pending BM confirmation of the real site ID —
73	 * see .docs/planning/regionalConfigSyncPlan.md).
74	 */
75	const COUNTRY_OVERLAY: Record<string, CountryOverlayEntry> = {
76	  au: { shippingCountry: 'AU', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'australia' },
77	  us: { shippingCountry: 'US', checkoutOwner: 'hybrid', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'usa' },
78	  'en-ca': { shippingCountry: 'CA', checkoutOwner: 'global-e', globalEPricing: true, boutiqueRegion: 'usa' }, // TBC — pending ZimmermannUSIntl
79	  uk: { shippingCountry: 'GB', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'uk' },
80	  'en-eu': { shippingCountry: 'DE', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'europe' }, // placeholder; shipping country resolved at checkout
81	  'fr-eu': { shippingCountry: 'FR', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'europe' },
82	  'it-eu': { shippingCountry: 'IT', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'europe' }, // placeholder; shipping country resolved at checkout
83	  'es-eu': { shippingCountry: 'ES', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'europe' }, // placeholder; shipping country resolved at checkout
84	  'en-ch': { shippingCountry: 'CH', checkoutOwner: 'global-e', globalEPricing: true, boutiqueRegion: 'europe' }, // placeholder; Global-e resolves shipping country
85	  hk: { shippingCountry: 'HK', checkoutOwner: 'global-e', globalEPricing: true, boutiqueRegion: 'hong-kong' },
86	  'en-ae': { shippingCountry: 'AE', checkoutOwner: 'global-e', globalEPricing: true, boutiqueRegion: 'middle-east' },
87	};
88	
89	/**
90	 * Keyed by urlSlug for O(1) lookup in routing/middleware.
91	 * AU is the exception: it has no URL prefix (root domain). Its key is 'au'
92	 * but urlSlug is '' — routing falls back to DEFAULT_COUNTRY_SLUG when no
93	 * prefix is detected.
94	 */
95	// Fail loud, not silent, if BM/the sync script produced a slug with no
96	// matching business-logic overlay — that means someone added a site to
97	// config/sites.overlay.js and ran `npm run sync:regional-config` without
98	// adding the corresponding COUNTRY_OVERLAY entry above. The reverse case
99	// (an overlay entry with no generated data yet, e.g. 'en-ca' pending the
100	// US-split site ID) is intentional and handled by the filter below instead.
101	const missingOverlays = Object.keys(GENERATED_COUNTRIES).filter((slug) => !(slug in COUNTRY_OVERLAY));
102	if (missingOverlays.length) {
103	  throw new Error(
104	    `countries.ts: config/sites.overlay.js has a site for slug(s) '${missingOverlays.join(', ')}' with no ` +
105	      `matching COUNTRY_OVERLAY entry — add shippingCountry/checkoutOwner/globalEPricing/boutiqueRegion for it.`,
106	  );
107	}
108	
109	export const COUNTRIES: Record<string, CountryConfig> = Object.fromEntries(
110	  Object.entries(COUNTRY_OVERLAY)
111	    .filter(([slug]) => slug in GENERATED_COUNTRIES)
112	    .map(([slug, overlay]) => [
113	      slug,
114	      {
115	        urlSlug: slug === 'au' ? '' : slug,
116	        ...(GENERATED_COUNTRIES as Record<string, { sfccSiteId: string; locale: string; currency: string }>)[slug],
117	        ...overlay,
118	      },
119	    ]),
120	);
121	
122	/** Fallback when no URL slug is present or IP detection fails. */
123	export const DEFAULT_COUNTRY_SLUG = 'au';
124	
125	/** Lookup by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code — used by IP-detection prompt. */
126	export const COUNTRY_BY_SHIPPING_CODE: Record<string, CountryConfig> = Object.fromEntries(
127	  Object.values(COUNTRIES).map((c) => [c.shippingCountry, c]),
128	);
129

content.text:
**Consequence first.** If we guess a country from browser language (Option 1), a French-speaking shopper in Belgium, Switzerland, or Canada could see "we noticed you're in France" — a factually wrong claim, sitting right next to an offer that's actually correct and useful (switch to the French-language site). The feature still *works* either way; only the flavor text risks being wrong.

**What this component is actually for.** Zimmermann runs one shared EU backend split into four separate storefronts by language — `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/`, `/en-eu/`. A shopper can land on the wrong one by accident — a shared link, an old bookmark, a search result — and their browser's language setting is a strong hint they're in the wrong place. The prompt's real job is just: "your browser says French, this site is Italian, want to switch?" That's the entire mechanism, and it works today regardless of how the copy is worded.

**Where `{inCountry}` actually came from — mechanism, not my invention.** This component has two variants: `location` (SFCC-823, not part of this build — detects the shopper's real *country*, presumably via geo-IP) and `language` (SFCC-689, what we're building — detects browser *language* only). The copy for both variants was written with shared framing — "we noticed you're [somewhere]" — but that framing only makes sense for the `location` variant, which actually has a country signal. The `language` variant's own trigger (REG-029, a deliberate decision to use browser language *instead of* geo-IP, made earlier in this exact engagement) structurally cannot produce a real country — browser language tells you what someone reads, not where they are. This is the same requirements tension already sitting in this build's own carried-forward open items (#11: "REG-031 contradicts REG-029... reads as a copy-paste error") — I didn't discover a new problem, I hit the edge of an already-known one while trying to actually wire up the code.

So the real question underneath my three options isn't really an engineering choice — it's: **does this prompt need to name a country at all, or is "your browser is set to French" reason enough on its own?** That's a copy/product call, not a technical one, which is why I paused instead of picking for you.

content.text:
You're right to question it, and the honest answer is: **you're not wrong to be only concerned with language — the country reference is a leftover from the original requirement text, not something the language-mismatch mechanism actually needs or can support.**

Here's exactly where it came from. `regional.languagePrompt.body`'s fallback — the text already shipped in B1 — reads: *"Welcome to Zimmermann Europe. We noticed you're {inCountry}, would you like to view our site {inLanguage}?"* That wording isn't something I invented while building the component; it directly follows **REG-031**, the requirement that literally prescribes: *"we noticed you're located in [detected country]."* So the language prompt's copy was written to match a requirement that assumes location-detection.

But the mechanism this build actually implements — **REG-029**, decided earlier in this same engagement — deliberately replaced geo-detection with browser-language detection for this exact prompt. When that switch was made, nobody went back and updated REG-031's prescribed wording to match. So today you have a requirement whose *copy* assumes we know the shopper's country, sitting next to a decision that *guarantees* we never will. That's not scope creep on my part; it's a pre-existing seam between two decisions that were made at different times, and I only hit it now because C3 is the step that has to actually produce a real value for `{inCountry}`, not just leave it as a placeholder in a fallback string.

So the real options, restated with that context:
- **Drop `{inCountry}` from the language variant entirely** — accept that "your browser is set to French" is reason enough on its own, no country needed. This is a genuine, small edit to *already-committed* B1 code: the `bodyFallback` string, the `inCountry` prop on `ZimmCountryLanguageMismatchLanguageProps`, and the seeded Contentful fallback in B2.
- **Guess a country from the language** (my earlier Option 1) — keeps REG-031's wording technically satisfied but risks telling a French-speaking Swiss or Belgian shopper they're "in France."
- **Add real geo-detection just for this one word** — real scope expansion nobody's asked for.

Given what you just said, dropping it sounds like the right call — the feature's entire job is language-switching, and manufacturing a country claim to satisfy a requirement that predates the trigger-mechanism decision seems like exactly the kind of thing REG-031 should be *corrected* for, not worked around in code. Want me to make that change to B1 (small, already-committed files) before building C3 on top of it?

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(regional): SFCC-689 match useCountryConfig on sfccSiteId

The four EU-domestic PWA sites (ZimmermannEUen/fr/it/es) share one real
SFCC site (ZimmermannEU), but useCountryConfig compared the config
table's sfccSiteId against the PWA site's own id — those only match by
coincidence on sites where the two are identical. Every EU-domestic
shopper was silently served the Australia config: wrong shipping
country, wrong boutique region, wrong checkout ownership.

The existing test suite didn't catch it because it mocked site.id as
'ZimmermannEU' — a value the real site config can never produce (that
string only ever appears as the separate sfccSiteId field). Corrected
the mocks to the real shape and demonstrated the fix red-before-green.

Also rewords a footer/index.tsx comment (Tier 2, comment-only) that
cited this exact buggy pattern as verified precedent for its own,
actually-correct-for-a-different-reason use of site.id.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -15
echo "---"
git log --oneline -1
git status --short

content.subject: A4 — fix ZimmDrawer prompt mobile height (bottom:auto)
content.description: prompt variant's height:'auto' never actually shrunk to content on mobile — position:fixed with top/right/bottom all pinned means height:auto stretches to fill, it doesn't shrink-wrap. Proven via real Playwright measurement at 440x956: panel rendered 898px tall (viewport-58), 572px of empty space below the last button. Fix: add bottom:'auto' to prompt's base-level content styles so top:0 anchors it and height:auto can actually shrink to content. maxHeight cap stays as a safety net. Only affects prompt (every other size sets an explicit height value, never relied on auto). Must be verified with a real rendered measurement, not just a recipe-value string assertion — that's exactly what let this bug ship undetected through A1.

Confirmed via fresh get_design_context on the real wrapping content-container node (I40002218:52408;40007204:171894): actual design is paddingInline 32px (--zimm-scale-2xl) + paddingBlock 48px (--zimm-scale-1200), not a uniform value. Marcel approved fixing both, accepting the shared-constant change affects Wishlist/Login/Find-in-Boutique/Cookies/Notify Me too. zm-implementer dispatched (agent a5e5c67f8e1e3a507).

content.subject: A6 — fix ZimmDrawer small header sizing (92px md+, matches Wishlist/Login)
content.description: Confirmed live: ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer (small variant) renders header at 80px at every breakpoint including tablet/desktop, same shape of bug prompt had before A5. small has no header override at md+ at all. Fix: add the same header override prompt got in A5 (minHeight:'unset', paddingBlock: HEADER_PADDING_Y at md+) — headerCloseButton plumbing already exists from A5, so this should be pure config. Marcel approved fixing now based on shared pdp/drawer component evidence (4-for-4 identical header chrome across Location/Language at every breakpoint), no Wishlist-specific Figma frame available.

content.text:
Direct answer: **drop it.** Given browser-language-only is confirmed as the trigger (no geo-detection), there's no honest value to put in `inCountry` — anything we place there is either a guess we can't back up, or a lie. The cleanest fix is removing the token from the copy entirely rather than inventing a value for it.

Concretely, the body sentence doesn't need it. The current shipped fallback is two clauses — "we noticed you're {inCountry}" (the part with no honest answer) and "would you like to view our site {inLanguage}" (the part that's true and useful). Dropping the first clause and keeping the second reads cleanly on its own:

> **Welcome to Zimmermann Europe.** Would you like to view our site in French?

That's `{inLanguage}` used exactly the way the switch CTA already uses it ("View {inLanguage}" → "View in French") — same token, same grammar, nothing new to invent.

This means touching three already-committed things, all small:
1. **`ZimmCountryLanguageMismatchLanguageProps`** (`index.tsx`, B1) — remove the `inCountry: string` field from the type.
2. **`VARIATION_CONFIG.language.bodyFallback`** (same file) — change to `'Would you like to view our site {inLanguage}?'`.
3. **`regional.languagePrompt.body`'s seeded value** (B2's seed script) — same wording change, so Contentful's English entry doesn't silently diverge from the new fallback (the seed script's own header comment already warns about exactly this).

`inCurrentLanguage` (used only in the "stay" CTA — "Continue in English") is untouched — it never referenced country in the first place.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__weave_get_tool_run_output
entries.description: Gets the output and status of runs of a Weave tool (a published Weave workflow). Pass the `recipeId` of the tool and the `runIds` returned by weave_run_tool; omit `runIds` to get the tool's most recent run. Returns each run's status (RUNNING, COMPLETED, FAILED, or CANCELED), progress, any error, and — when complete — a link to every output the run produced. Poll this after running a tool to track progress and read its output. Each output is a JSON entry with a `url`, its `type` (e.g. image, video), and, when known, `width`/`height`/`format`. The response also includes curl instructions for downloading the outputs — the URL+curl path is strongly preferred because it uses far fewer tokens than embedding media inline.

recipeId.description: The id of the Weave tool whose runs to fetch (from weave_list_tools).

runIds.description: The run ids to fetch output for, as returned by weave_run_tool. Omit to use the tool's most recent run (the latest in-flight run, or the latest completed run's output if none are in flight).

entries.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:

entries.name: LSP
entries.description:
Interact with Language Server Protocol (LSP) servers to get code intelligence features.

Supported operations:
- goToDefinition: Find where a symbol is defined
- findReferences: Find all references to a symbol
- hover: Get hover information (documentation, type info) for a symbol
- documentSymbol: Get all symbols (functions, classes, variables) in a document
- workspaceSymbol: Search for symbols matching a query across the entire workspace
- goToImplementation: Find implementations of an interface or abstract method
- prepareCallHierarchy: Get call hierarchy item at a position (functions/methods)
- incomingCalls: Find all functions/methods that call the function at a position
- outgoingCalls: Find all functions/methods called by the function at a position

All operations require:
- filePath: The file to operate on
- line: The line number (1-based, as shown in editors)
- character: The character offset (1-based, as shown in editors)

The workspaceSymbol operation also takes:
- query: The symbol name or partial name to search for. Always provide it — most language servers return no results for an empty query.

Note: LSP servers must be configured for the file type. If no server is available, an error will be returned.

line.description: The line number (1-based, as shown in editors)

character.description: The character offset (1-based, as shown in editors)

content.text:
Let me trace it end to end with a concrete example, since that's the clearest way to show it.

**Scenario:** a shopper is on `/en-eu/` (the English EU site), and their browser reports French.

**Step 1 — detection (already built, C1).** `shouldShowLanguagePrompt` compares the browser's language against the current site's language, finds a mismatch, and returns `{ show: true, targetLanguage: 'fr' }`. No country involved — this was never geo-detection to begin with, just a language-code comparison.

**Step 2 — turning codes into display phrases (C3's job).** The container needs to turn `'fr'` into the phrase `"in French"`, and the *current* site's own language (`'en-GB'`) into `"in English"`. This needs one small, fixed lookup table — but critically, it's a **language → phrase** map, not a language → country map: `fr → "in French"`, `it → "in Italian"`, `es → "in Spanish"`, `en → "in English"`. There's no ambiguity here the way there was with country — "fr" unambiguously means "French" the language; it only got murky when we tried to also claim a *country* from it (France? Belgium? Switzerland?). This lookup was already unavoidable regardless of the `{inCountry}` decision — the CTA button already needs it to render "View in French."

**Step 3 — interpolation (already built, `useUiCopy`).** Nothing about this mechanism changes. `t('regional.languagePrompt.body', 'Would you like to view our site {inLanguage}?', { inLanguage: 'in French' })` finds `{inLanguage}` in the template and substitutes it. Since the new template has no `{inCountry}` slot at all, there's nothing left to compute, guess, or leave blank for country — it's simply not part of the sentence anymore.

**Step 4 — what actually renders:**
- Heading: *"Welcome to Zimmermann Europe"*
- Body: *"Would you like to view our site in French?"*
- Switch CTA: *"View in French"*
- Stay CTA: *"Continue in English"*

Nothing about `inCurrentLanguage` changes in this discussion either — it was always derived from the *current* site's own known language, never from geo-detection, so it was never affected by any of this.

Net effect: dropping `{inCountry}` doesn't add any new lookup or logic — it removes the one piece (country) that had no clean, unambiguous source. The one lookup C3 does need (language code → phrase) was already required for the CTAs regardless of this decision.

content.text:
Here's the concrete shape of it — including the part that doesn't resolve cleanly.

**The map itself, one entry per supported language:**
```ts
const LANGUAGE_TO_COUNTRY_PHRASE: Record<string, string> = {
  fr: 'in France',
  it: 'in Italy',
  es: 'in Spain',
  en: ???,  // no clean answer — see below
};
```
Used at the point C3 builds the props: `inCountry={LANGUAGE_TO_COUNTRY_PHRASE[detectedLanguage]}`.

**Three of the four are clean.** French→France, Italian→Italy, Spanish→Spain are obvious, low-risk guesses.

**The fourth doesn't have a good answer, and this matters because it's a real, common case.** EU domestic's English site (`en-eu`) isn't the UK site — it's a separate, fourth language option alongside fr/it/es. "English" doesn't map to one EU country the way French maps to France. The candidates: "in the UK" (wrong — UK isn't in the EU, and isn't the same site as `en-eu`), "in Ireland" (the actual EU member state where English is a home language, but a strange guess for most people to see), or breaking the pattern entirely for just this one case (adds a special-cased branch instead of a clean uniform lookup). There's no option here that isn't visibly odd to at least some real shoppers.

**And even the "clean" three aren't actually safe.** A Belgian or Swiss French-speaker sees "in France." A Swiss Italian-speaker sees "in Italy." A French-Canadian sees "in France" too (though that population mostly wouldn't reach these sites in the first place — they have their own site). These aren't rare edge cases for a European audience specifically — Belgium and Switzerland both have real French- and Italian-speaking populations likely to actually hit an EU-domestic Zimmermann storefront.

**One more cost worth naming:** this map would need to live somewhere and stay in sync with `shouldShowLanguagePrompt.ts`'s own `SUPPORTED_EU_LANGUAGES` list (already `['en','fr','it','es']` from C1) — a second thing to remember to update together, and a standing risk that someone later mistakes it for real geo-data and "fixes" the English case by bolting on actual detection, when the whole thing was only ever meant to be a stand-in.

So the honest picture: this option satisfies REG-031's literal wording for 3 of 4 languages, at the cost of being confidently wrong for real subpopulations in all four, with the fourth case having no answer that isn't awkward on its face.
