entries.description: Get variable definitions for a given node id. E.g. {'icon/default/secondary': #949494}Variables are reusable values that can be applied to all kinds of design properties, such as fonts, colors, sizes and spacings. Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id. Extract the node id from the URL, for example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=1-2, the extracted nodeId would be `1:2`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, ask the user for a node-specific URL. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. This remote tool requires a concrete node target. This tool is not supported for Figma Make Files (URLs containing `/make/`). If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`. Only design files are supported: the URL must be a /design/ URL. /slides/, /board/, and /make/ URLs are not allowed.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__search_design_system
entries.description:
Search for design system assets (components, variables, and styles) based on a text query. Returns matching assets from all design libraries. Use this when you need to find specific components, variables (e.g. colors, spacing tokens), or styles from design libraries.
To combine searches already required for the task, pass a `queries` array in one call instead of issuing multiple calls; never add speculative terms, synonyms, variants, or checklist items to fill a batch. Results are keyed by query text. Provide either `query` or `queries`, not both.

query.description: Deprecated for new callers; prefer `queries` with one entry. A text query describing one design-system asset to find. Use a specific component, variable, or style name, or a short natural-language phrase. Multi-word names and phrases are allowed. Each query MUST express exactly one search intent. You MUST NOT combine alternatives, synonyms, or unrelated searches in one query; this tool does NOT apply OR semantics. To run several independent searches, pass them as separate entries in `queries` instead of making one call each.

queries.description: Run multiple design-system searches in one call instead of issuing separate calls per term. Each entry must specify `entity` as component, variable, or style, and must be an asset already identified as needed for the current task, exactly as `query` would be. Do not add speculative terms, generic checklists, synonyms, or naming variants to fill a batch. Use one batched call instead of parallel tool calls. Inspect results before deciding on a follow-up, and do not treat an empty result as a reason to try alternate terms. Provide EITHER query OR queries, not both. Results are returned in the same order as the entries.

entity.description: The design-system entity type to search for this entry.

query.description: Text query describing one design-system asset of the specified entity type to find.

fileKey.description: The file key for context

disableCodeConnect.description: Whether to disable Code Connect for search results.

includeComponents.description: For single-query calls, whether to include components in the search results. Defaults to true. Batch calls use each entry entity instead.

includeVariables.description: For single-query calls, whether to include variables in the search results. Defaults to true. Batch calls use each entry entity instead.

includeStyles.description: For single-query calls, whether to include styles in the search results. Defaults to true. Batch calls use each entry entity instead.

includeLibraryKeys.description: Optional list of library keys to restrict the search to. When provided, only results from these libraries are returned. Library keys are returned in previous search results.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__use_figma
entries.description:
Create, edit, generate, or sync any design in Figma — UIs, screens, mockups, components, frames, variables, styles, text, images, layouts, and design systems. This general-purpose tool writes to Figma with JavaScript via the Figma Plugin API. Works on Figma design files (URL path `/design/`), FigJam boards (`/board/`), and Figma Slides (`/slides/`).

IMPORTANT: Before calling this tool, load figma-use guidance — prefer the /figma-use skill if available, otherwise read the skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md MCP resource if available. Skipping this causes common, hard-to-debug failures.

Use this tool when the user wants to:
- Create or generate a Figma design, screen, UI, or mockup from scratch, intent, or code
- Update, edit, or sync an existing Figma design
- Generate or sync Figma designs from source code
- Set up or modify design tokens, variables, or styles
- Build or extend a design system or component/variant library
- Fix layout, spacing, auto-layout, or fill/hug issues
- Add component descriptions, annotations and Code Connect metadata to nodes
- Review or fix accessibility, contrast, typography, or visual polish
- Inspect or query node properties programmatically
CHOOSING BETWEEN use_figma AND generate_figma_design:
- Default to use_figma for all write operations
- Exception: generate_figma_design ONLY to capture a web app page/view for the first time. For web apps, run both in parallel — generate_figma_design captures a pixel-perfect screenshot, use_figma builds from imported design system components and refines against the screenshot
- Non-web (iOS, Android, generic UI) and from-scratch designs: use_figma only
- Updating/syncing a Figma page already captured: use_figma — even if source code changed
GOTCHAS
- For the font "Inter", the style is "Semi Bold", not "SemiBold" and "Extra Bold" not "ExtraBold"
- MUST use `await figma.setCurrentPageAsync(page)` to change pages. Setting figma.currentPage is not supported
- MUST NEVER use loadAllPagesAsync,setPluginData,createImageAsync. They are not supported API

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

code.description: JavaScript code to execute. Has access to the `figma` global (Figma Plugin API)

description.description: A concise description of what the code aims to do

skillNames.description: A comma-separated list of Figma skill names being followed, if any (e.g. "figma-use", "figma-use,figma-generate-design"). Only pass this when explicitly instructed to by skill documentation. Used for logging purposes. If the skill was loaded via a skill-content MCP resource, prefix the skill name with "resource:". (e.g. "resource:figma-use", "resource:figma-use,resource:figma-generate-design")

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__weave_get_tool_inputs
entries.description: Gets the input contract of a Weave tool (a published Weave workflow) — the inputs you fill in to run it. Pass the `recipeId` (from weave_list_tools, or the `<id>` in a pasted Weave URL like app.weavy.ai/tool/<id> or app.weavy.ai/flow/<id> — that `<id>` is the recipeId). A pasted Weave URL is enough to inspect and run the tool right here — do not open a browser or use browser automation for Weave. Call this before weave_run_tool to learn what to send. Returns the tool `version` (pass it back to weave_run_tool), an `outputs` summary (what the tool produces), and a flat `inputs` list. Each input has a `nodeId` (the key you send in weave_run_tool), `name`, `type` (text, integer, boolean, select, seed, image, video, audio, 3D, color, or any), `default` (its current value), and `required` (true only when there is no current value, so you must provide one), plus `options` (for `select`), `range`, `isIterator`, and `description`.

recipeId.description: The id of the Weave tool whose input contract to fetch — from weave_list_tools, or the `<id>` in a pasted Weave URL (app.weavy.ai/tool/<id> or app.weavy.ai/flow/<id>), which is the recipeId.

version.description: Tool version to inspect; omit for the latest.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__weave_get_tool_run_output
entries.description: Gets the output and status of runs of a Weave tool (a published Weave workflow). Pass the `recipeId` of the tool and the `runIds` returned by weave_run_tool; omit `runIds` to get the tool's most recent run. Returns each run's status (RUNNING, COMPLETED, FAILED, or CANCELED), progress, any error, and — when complete — a link to every output the run produced. Poll this after running a tool to track progress and read its output. Each output is a JSON entry with a `url`, its `type` (e.g. image, video), and, when known, `width`/`height`/`format`. The response also includes curl instructions for downloading the outputs — the URL+curl path is strongly preferred because it uses far fewer tokens than embedding media inline.

recipeId.description: The id of the Weave tool whose runs to fetch (from weave_list_tools).

runIds.description: The run ids to fetch output for, as returned by weave_run_tool. Omit to use the tool's most recent run (the latest in-flight run, or the latest completed run's output if none are in flight).

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__weave_list_tools
entries.description: Lists the Weave tools the authenticated user can run — published Weave workflows — in their active Weave workspace: their own, those shared with the workspace, and those shared with them directly. Here "tool" means a Weave tool (a published Weave workflow), not an agent/MCP tool. Use this when the user wants to see, browse, or choose from the Weave tools available to them. Returns the most recently updated tools and the total number available, each with its name, who created it, when it was last updated, and a link to open it in Weave. If the user already pasted a specific Weave URL (app.weavy.ai/tool/<id> or app.weavy.ai/flow/<id>), you already have its recipeId — that `<id>` — so skip this and go straight to weave_get_tool_inputs/weave_run_tool instead of opening a browser.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against tool names, to look up a tool the user named.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__weave_run_tool
entries.description: Runs a Weave tool (a published Weave workflow) and returns run ids; poll them with weave_get_tool_run_output. A pasted Weave URL (app.weavy.ai/tool/<id> or app.weavy.ai/flow/<id>) is enough — never open a browser or use browser automation for Weave. Call weave_get_tool_inputs first to learn the inputs. This tool spends the user's Weave credits, so it is gated: it returns `status: "inputs_required"` or `cost_confirmation_required` with instructions to follow. Always show the user the cost and get an explicit Approve/Cancel (a structured prompt, not free text) before echoing `acknowledgedCost` to run — every run, including reruns — and confirm any auto-filled inputs (values you did not set that the run will use). Include the response's `costDisclosure` string as its own sentence after the question, not folded into it, the first time you quote a cost in a conversation; omit it after that. For an image/video input, pass a reachable https URL directly; only upload a local file with weave_upload_asset and pass the asset object it returns. If the user wants an input you did not get from weave_get_tool_inputs, do not omit it or fold it into another input like the prompt — re-fetch weave_get_tool_inputs (its inputs can change) and set it.

recipeId.description: The id of the Weave tool to run — from weave_list_tools, or the `<id>` in a pasted Weave URL (app.weavy.ai/tool/<id> or app.weavy.ai/flow/<id>), which is the recipeId.

version.description: The tool `version` from weave_get_tool_inputs; omit to run the latest.

inputs.description: Values for the inputs you want to set. Omit an input to keep its current value.

nodeId.description: The input's `nodeId` from weave_get_tool_inputs.

value.description: The value for this input, in the shape for its `type` (from weave_get_tool_inputs): text→string, integer→number, boolean→true/false, select→one of its `options`, seed→a number (or omit this input for random), image/video→a reachable https URL, color→a hex string like "#RRGGBB" (or a list of them), an iterator→an array of values (runs once per item).

numberOfRuns.description: How many times to run the tool (1–10).

acknowledgedCost.description: The credit `cost` the tool quoted in its `cost_confirmation_required` response, echoed back after the user approves to confirm the spend and run. For a dynamic-cost tool (the response had `isDynamicCost: true` and `cost: null`), pass `-1` to confirm a variable charge.

PostBuild audit's done — full writeup is in `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-831/postbuild.md`. Here's the whole thing.

## 1. Diff summary

15 commits on `feature/SFCC-831-689_country-language-mismatch` (base `develop`@`2510cea`, head `ba73b20`), 34 files.

- **Tier 1: zero.** Nothing in `theme/foundation/`, no config, no CI. This was the gate's own biggest fear ("possibly T1") and it never materialized.
- **Tier 2: 5 files**, all small — a recipe registration, a comment reword, the two-line `_app` mount + its test, and one comment-only line in `zimmDrawerShared.ts`.
- **Tier 3 / untiered:** everything else — the new component, hooks, utils, and 4 Contentful seed scripts.

## 2. Audit result

**findings.md (27 gate rows):** all 4 blockers held through the shipped code. Of the 13 CLARIFY assumptions, 10 held as stated, 3 didn't hold *exactly* but resolved to something better or more precise (not worse) — e.g. the cookie helper grew from ~15 lines to 168 for good, named reasons, and the "who translates copy" question got the engineering half solved (seeded, live) while the actual translation-pipeline trigger is now precisely identified as `TBD` in this project's own docs, not just "unresolved." Nothing regressed.

**plan.md vs. the real diff:** every one of the 25 manifest files shipped, at the tier the plan said. One thing slipped through the paperwork: `zimmDrawerShared.ts` got a real, if comment-only, Tier 2 touch during A5 that nobody ever explicitly logged as a Tier 2 file — B1 and C3 both checked "no extra Tier 2 file showed up" and both were technically wrong by one line of comment. Zero functional consequence, but I've named it in the PR body so CODEOWNERS' reviewer request on it doesn't land as a surprise. Also caught a small citation error in `handoff.md` (credits the plan with a phrase the plan never actually said) — harmless, corrected in the record.

## 3. Sweep result — UNIFORM first

This is the part a step-by-step review structurally can't see.

**U1 (the one that matters):** the exact same English copy string is hand-typed in up to **4 separate places** — the two Contentful seed scripts, the component's own fallback config, its stories, and its test — held in sync by nothing but a code comment. Two of those four are a real risk (Contentful's field could silently drift from the code's fallback and nothing would catch it); the other two are lower-risk because a drift there is either visible in Storybook or fails a test loudly. Not fixed here — that's Build's job if you want it addressed — but the fix direction is cheap: the language-key sync test already exists for keys, just extend it to cover values too.

Five smaller ONE-OFF findings, worth naming quickly:
- Two stale comments (one about a header-height constant's consumer count, one hardcoding `2.75rem` instead of importing the constant that's already imported two lines away).
- A comment in the *existing* Wishlist drawer's test file that was true when written and became false three commits later, once this build added the first-ever test to the base `ZimmDrawer` — the kind of thing only an aggregate view catches.
- The canonical Figma node for the Language/Mobile variant itself still has a stray third button contradicting your own team's already-decided 2-button call — that's a Figma file cleanup item, not a code defect; confirmed the shipped code only ever renders 2 buttons.
- A defensible judgment call on one `useEffect`'s complexity — flagged, not a violation.

Everything else checked out clean by direct comparison — recipe shapes, token reuse, `site.id` vs `site.sfccSiteId` semantics across all 3 real call sites, and all 15 story×breakpoint combinations re-measured live against Figma.

## 4. Proposed PR

**Title:** `feat(regional): SFCC-831/689 EU country/language mismatch prompt`

Body follows the real house format (confirmed off PR #59, not the stale template my memory had): `Description` / `Linked` / `Squad ownership` / `Types of Changes` / `Changes` / `How to test-drive this PR` / `Protection-tier check` / `Testing`. Full text is in `postbuild.md` — it names the two deliberately-deferred items (location variant has no live trigger yet; who translates the new copy going forward is still an open TransPerfect-side question), the 5 Tier 2 touches with reasoning, and the real test numbers (870/823/47 lint baseline exactly matching `develop`, all suites green, 9 Contentful entries live in `dev`).

## 5. Could not verify

- A real SFCC storefront name longer than any fixture this build tested against (button clipping is safe with 31% margin against everything actually tested — not against every name that could ever exist).
- Whether the 9 Contentful entries have been seeded anywhere beyond `dev`.
- A real click-through cross-site navigation in an actual browser — deliberately left for you.

## What Marcel is missing

The suppression cookie writing unconditionally, independent of Didomi consent state, is still an open question nobody has actually decided — the gate flagged it as "will be re-litigated at PR review," and it genuinely hasn't been re-litigated by anyone since, including me. It's real: this repo's own consent rule says fail closed / gate all tracking behind Didomi, and while a preference cookie isn't a tracking script, it's also not obviously exempt. I've left it as an explicit open line in the PR body rather than silently deciding it either way — but if it doesn't get a real answer at review, it'll ship by default rather than by choice. If you don't raise it yourself, I'll flag it again the moment a reviewer comment doesn't address it.

Everything's written up, nothing's pushed, no PR is open. Say go and I'll push the branch and open it.

## The sweep findings — consequence → mechanism → fix

The "audit" (Phase 1) checked whether the plan was followed. The "sweep" (Phase 2) is different — it looks across the *whole* finished feature for a pattern that's wrong everywhere consistently, which a step-by-step review can never catch because each step only ever compares its own patch against its own criteria. Here's everything it found.

### 🟡 U1 — Copy typed by hand in 4 places, nothing keeps them in sync

**Consequence:** someone edits the component's English fallback text (or the Contentful entry) without touching the other, and now the CMS value and the code's own fallback silently disagree. A shopper on a locale that falls back to English sees stale or wrong copy. No test fails, nothing warns anyone — you'd only find out by eyeballing the live site.

**Mechanism:** the same strings exist in 4 separate files — the component's own config, the Contentful seed script, the Storybook stories, and the test file. The only thing telling a future editor "these have to match" is a code comment. Comments don't get enforced by the compiler or the test runner.

**Fix (not done — this is Build's call if you want it):** the codebase already has the right pattern next door — there's a test that keeps the language *keys* in sync between two config objects. Extend that same idea to cover the actual *values*, and have the seed scripts import from the component's config instead of retyping it. Two of the four spots (the seed scripts) are the real risk; the other two (stories, test file) are lower-stakes because a drift there either shows up visibly in Storybook or fails a test loudly instead of silently.

### 🔵 Four smaller one-offs

**1. A stale comment that undersells its own file's risk.** `zimmDrawer.css.ts:299` says a constant is "only consumed by xLarge." This build's own A6 step made `small` a second consumer and nobody updated the sentence. Consequence: low today, but the next person to touch that constant reads a wrong picture of the blast radius. Fix: one-line comment edit, whenever that file's next touched.

**2. A test that can't catch its own regression.** `zimmDrawer.css.test.ts:112` hardcodes `'2.75rem'` instead of importing the constant it's testing against — a constant the same file already imports two lines away for a different assertion. Consequence: if that constant's real value ever changes, this specific test keeps passing with the old number, giving false confidence. Fix: swap the literal for the import. Trivial.

**3. The one genuinely interesting catch — a comment that became false because of *this build*, in a file this build didn't even touch for that reason.** `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.test.tsx:8` says "the component itself has no test yet." True the day it was written. Three commits later, this build's A3 step gave the base `ZimmDrawer` its first-ever test — and that sentence quietly became a lie, because no single step's own review was ever going to re-check an unrelated file's old comment. This is exactly the class of thing a whole-feature sweep exists to catch. Consequence: someone reads it, believes there's zero coverage, and either duplicates it or makes a change trusting nothing will catch a break. Fix: delete the sentence.

**4. Figma file itself, not code — a stray 3rd button.** The canonical Language/Mobile design node still has a leftover placeholder button, even though the team already ratified "this component only ever has 2 CTAs" a while back. Confirmed via real screenshots that the shipped component only ever renders 2 buttons — so this changes nothing about what ships. It's a design-file tidiness item for whoever owns that Figma file, not an engineering task.

One judgment call, not a defect: `ZimmLanguagePrompt`'s one `useEffect` does slightly more than a one-liner, which is one of this repo's own triggers for "consider extracting to a hook." Leaving it as-is is defensible — all the actual decision logic already lives in a separately-tested pure function, so the effect itself is basically just calling that function and reacting. Worth revisiting only if more logic gets added to it later.

**Everything else checked out clean** — recipe shapes match across every drawer variant, no token is typed twice, `site.id` vs `site.sfccSiteId` is used correctly at all 3 real call sites, and all 15 story×breakpoint combinations were re-measured live against Figma and matched exactly.

Nothing here rises to "hand it back to Build" — it's all paperwork/hygiene, not a functional break. Still waiting on your go to push and open the PR.

The executor. Takes an approved plan and builds it, one step at a time, with every step tested,
scope-checked, scored and seen by Marcel before it becomes a commit.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — the loop
agents are pinned to Sonnet in their own frontmatter regardless.

**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get the full loop. The plan states the scale it
chose and why; honour it. Over-scaled machinery is a defect, not thoroughness. Nothing too crazy,
no overthinking.

**Report in "ELI5BITFEDLOTP" register** — Explain Like I'm 5, But I'm The FED Lead Of The
Project. Not dumbed down, but no jargon that gets in the way: lead with the consequence, then the
mechanism, then the fix. This is the default for everything you put in front of Marcel unless he
asks for a different level.

---

and executes it. This is the default.

**`rework`** — invoked as `rework <TICKET>` after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has
requested changes. Skips planning entirely; see the last section.

If no plan exists for the ticket, stop and say so. **Do not plan here** — that is
`zimmerMANNPreBuild`'s job, and building from an unplanned story is how an afternoon gets burned
on the wrong thing.

---

## Before the first step

1. Confirm the branch. **Not `develop`, not `main`** — a `PreToolUse` hook blocks every Write and
   Edit there. If the branch is wrong, stop.
2. Confirm the working tree is clean, or that everything dirty is expected and belongs to this
   story. Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.
3. Read the plan's file manifest, tiers and per-step pass criteria. **Any file marked BLOCKED
   stops the run** until Marcel confirms owner approval.
4. Record the baseline: run the four per-step gates now and note the numbers. A gate that is
   non-zero at baseline is not a failure you introduced.

---

## The loop — once per step

```
Implementer  →  Tester  →  Orchestrator  →  Scorer  →  [Marcel]  →  commit
                   ↑                          │
                   └────── REWORK, max 3 ─────┘
```

**1. `zm-implementer`** builds the step. Only the files the step names. It never stages and never
commits.

**2. `zm-tester`** fans out its own angle sub-agents, re-pointed for this step, and reports
findings with CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE and UNIFORM/ONE-OFF labels, plus what it tried to falsify and
what it could not verify.

**3. `zm-orchestrator`** returns a scope verdict — IN SCOPE / UNDER / OVER / BLOCKED. Under and
over carry equal weight.

**4. `zm-scorer`** takes both and scores six axes. PASS or REWORK.

**REWORK returns to the Implementer with a specific instruction. Maximum three rounds.** On the
third, stop and surface to Marcel — three failures means the plan or the criteria are wrong, not
the implementation.

**A step prompt may narrow what an agent looks at. It may never contradict that agent's brief, and
it may never pre-answer the question the agent exists to ask.** Before dispatching, read the prompt
against the brief. If you are telling the Implementer not to stop and ask, telling the Orchestrator
which files to leave out of the manifest check, or handing the Tester a measurement to treat as
given, you have disabled the agent while still collecting its verdict. All three have happened: one
build's step prompts carried "do not stop and ask, do not leave a TODO" against a stop-and-ratify
rule added to `zm-implementer.md` days earlier, and another narrowed the Orchestrator's diff by
instruction, then relayed its "IN SCOPE, clean" onward — where PostBuild's own Orchestrator later
returned OVER on that same diff.

**If a narrowing is genuinely wanted, carry it into the verdict you relay.** "IN SCOPE, against a
manifest I restricted" is a usable answer. "IN SCOPE, clean" is not.

### Per-step gates — the cheap four

Run every step. Seconds each.

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test                        # includes recipeGuards, the hard styling gate
npm run lint                        # compare counts, not the exit code
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs    # new unacknowledged findings only
```

Two traps: `npm run lint` exits non-zero at a healthy baseline, so **compare the count against
your baseline and ignore the exit code**. And never append arguments to it — `pwa-kit-dev lint`
forwards `--`-args into `execSync`, which can silently turn the gate into a writer.

The plan's per-step pass criteria layer **on top of** these, they do not replace them.

### The visual checkpoint

**After any step that changes rendered output, the loop stops.** The plan marks which steps those
are; if it doesn't, assume any step touching a component, a recipe or a page does.

Tell Marcel exactly:
- the URL and the viewport to open
- the Figma node to compare against — the one for **that variant and state**
- what should be on screen
- what would indicate a defect, including anything that will look wrong but is correct

Then **wait.** Do not proceed on assumption. This is the only gate on this stack that catches a
layout defect — `width: 'xl'` passed every automated check and destroyed the global footer.

Until it has happened, the Scorer's Design fidelity axis is UNVERIFIED, not passed.

### The commit

**The skill commits, not an agent.** Only after: Scorer PASS, and the visual checkpoint passed if
one was owed.

**State the provenance in the commit turn, or do not commit.** Name the step, which loop agents
actually ran for it, the Scorer's verdict and round, and the visual checkpoint's outcome. Any of
those that did not happen is written as **"did not run"** in those words — and a commit carrying
`did not run` against the Scorer, or against an owed visual checkpoint, stops for Marcel's
explicit override instead of proceeding. The loop collapsing into one inline agent is the most
expensive failure this skill has: it is invisible from inside, and re-reading this file mid-build
does not restore it. Only a per-commit statement makes it visible while it is still happening.

One step, one commit. Conventional Commits — the `commit-msg` hook enforces it. **No Claude
attribution, no CodeRabbit mentions, no `Co-Authored-By` line.** Use Marcel's previously authored
commits on this repo as the reference for tone and body.

Then move to the next step.

---

## Before handing off

Once every step has passed, run the expensive gates **once**:

```
npm run build-storybook             # then run the interaction + a11y suite against it
npm run test:story                  # real BrowserStack, scoped to the Jira key
npm run test:max-file-size          # runs a full build
cr review --base develop            # CodeRabbit locally, full review before anything is public
```

Storybook needs a verified-free port and a build you can prove is yours — a stale server on 6006
produced a silently meaningless pass once. Check the served build matches your own before trusting
any result.

Then **write the handoff** to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/handoff.md`:

```
# Handoff — <TICKET>
Branch: <branch>   Base: <sha>   Head: <sha>

## Steps
| # | What | Commit | Scorer verdict | Rework rounds |

## Gates (real numbers, not claims)
| Gate | Result | Baseline |

## UNIFORM findings
<each one, with file:line — these are what a per-step review structurally cannot catch>

## Could not verify
<named, with why>

## Outstanding
<anything left, or "none">
```

**Write it even when everything passed** — and do not wait until here to start it. Create the file
at the first commit and append its Steps row on every commit thereafter, so it exists even when a
build never formally reaches this section. PostBuild reads this file, and it may run in a
different session — a handoff that exists only in conversation does not survive the session
ending.

This is not hypothetical: `handoff.md` exists for one story in ten. The trigger above is
unreachable in exactly the builds that most need it, because it sits behind "once every step has
passed" and a collapsed loop never passes a step. Its absence is not neutral — PostBuild infers
from a missing handoff that the loop never ran, and wrote exactly that into a durable artefact for
a build whose Scorer verdicts were recoverable from the subagent transcripts all along.

Then present the same content to Marcel and **hand off to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`. This skill does
not push and does not open a PR.**

---

## Rework mode

Entered after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has requested changes.

**Read `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/postbuild.md` first.** It records what earlier rounds
already declined and why. A finding that was declined with evidence in round one does not get
re-litigated in round three — check before you verify anything, and if you disagree with a previous
decline, say so rather than silently reversing it.

**1. Verify every finding before touching anything.** CodeRabbit has been wrong on this repo
often — one batch ran 1-in-6 correct. Treat each finding as a hypothesis, not a fact. Per finding:

- **VALID** — reproduce it, cite `file:line`, fix it
- **INVALID** — say what is actually true, with the evidence, and draft the reply
- **OUT OF SCOPE** — real but not this story's problem; name the owning ticket or the person
- **DEFER** — real, in scope, but blocked on a decision; name who decides

**2. Fix only the VALID ones.** Same rules as build mode — the Implementer touches only what the
finding names, never stages, never commits.

**3. Re-run the cheap four**, plus the visual checkpoint if the fix changes rendered output.

**4. Commit the fixes here**, same rule as build mode — the skill commits, never an agent. Reference
the review thread each commit answers.

**5. Hand back to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`** with: what was fixed and in which commit, what was
declined and why, and the evidence behind each decline. **PostBuild owns the push and the
in-thread replies** — every finding gets a written answer, including the declined ones.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never push. Never open or update a PR.** That boundary belongs to PostBuild, which presents
  first and pushes only once Marcel has given the go.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never touch a Tier 1 file** without Marcel naming it and confirming owner approval.
- **Never expand scope.** Something worth doing that the plan didn't ask for gets reported, not
  done. Report it and let Marcel decide.
- **Local-only docs are never citable** in a commit message or a code comment. Cite `AGENTS.md`
  or `.claude/rules/*` instead.
- **Say what you could not verify.** Silence reads as "nothing wrong" when it may mean
  "didn't look there".

---

## What Marcel is missing

Close every report with this section. Always, even when it is one line.

This is **not** "what I could not verify" — that is your own blind spot and it has its own home.
This is his: something he has not thought to ask about, a decision he is about to make on a stale
premise, a risk sitting just outside this task that you can see from where you are standing, or a
call that genuinely needs him rather than you. Name it, say why it needs him, and say what you
will do if he says nothing.

Write "nothing this pass" only when you have actually gone looking. This is the one section where
a blank is itself a claim.

Finding 4a and 4b both ask for `import { ENTRIES } from '~/scripts/contentful/seed*.mjs'` inside a strict-mode `.tsx` test file. Nobody has imported a plain `.mjs` file into TypeScript here before, and `tsconfig.json` has no `allowJs`/`checkJs` anywhere in it. Under `strict: true`, that means the import itself is a compile error (TS7016 — "could not find a declaration file"), and it cascades into a second error on the `.find()` callback parameter (TS7006). I tried both the static form and a dynamic `await import()` form — identical failure either way, so it's not an import-style problem, it's that this repo's TS surface simply doesn't extend to plain `.js`/`.mjs` files at all, for anyone.

content.text:
## The core problem, plainly

This repo has two separate worlds:

- **App code** (everything under `overrides/`) — TypeScript, strictly type-checked. Nothing compiles unless every import's shape is known.
- **The Contentful seed scripts** — plain JavaScript (`.mjs`), run directly by `node`, never type-checked by anything.

The fix for finding 4 needs one test that reaches across that boundary — it reads the real copy from the component (TypeScript world) and the real copy from the seed script (JavaScript world) and checks they match. That's the whole point: an actual check, not a comment asking nicely.

TypeScript's strict mode won't let a `.tsx` file import a plain `.js`/`.mjs` file without being told what's inside it first — because by default it has no way to know. That's the wall the implementer hit. Here are the ways through it.

## Option 1 — flip a global switch (`allowJs`) in the project's shared TypeScript rulebook

**Consequence:** fixes it everywhere, instantly. But it also permanently changes what "this compiles" means for the *entire* project, not just these two files — from now on, TypeScript starts inspecting every plain `.js` file anything imports, project-wide, forever.

**Mechanism:** `tsconfig.json` is the one rulebook every single file in the app compiles against. It's on the frozen list specifically because a change there never stays local — it's a blast-radius problem by design, not a technicality.

**Why not this one:** we need 2 files understood. This option makes TypeScript start caring about every `.js` file in the whole repo. Way too big a lever for the job.

## Option 2 — write the shape down once, in one small new file (my recommendation)

**Consequence:** TypeScript is told, in exactly one place, "these two specific files export an array shaped like this." Everything else in the repo compiles exactly as it did yesterday — nothing else even notices this file exists unless it imports one of those two scripts.

**Mechanism:** this codebase already does this exact trick once. There's a file called `vendor.d.ts` that exists because a couple of installed packages don't ship their own type information — someone wrote, by hand, "here's what this package looks like," and TypeScript trusts it from then on. I'd do the identical thing for our two seed scripts instead of a downloaded package: a few lines, one new small file.

**Why this one:** smallest possible footprint, doesn't touch anything frozen, doesn't change how any other file compiles, and — unlike the next option — the test still gets a *real, checked* type on the data it's comparing, not a shrug.

## Option 3 — tell TypeScript to look away at that one line

**Consequence:** the error disappears, but the data coming through that import is now untyped — TypeScript just stops checking it at all from that point on.

**Mechanism:** there's a comment (`@ts-expect-error`) that silences one specific error at one specific line. This codebase already uses it twice, but only for two narrow reasons, neither of which is "I'm importing plain JS and TypeScript can't see inside it." Using it here invents a third reason with nothing backing it up.

**Why not this one:** same amount of effort as option 2, strictly worse outcome — option 2 costs one small file and gets you a real type; this costs one comment and gets you no type at all.

## Option 4 — don't chase this one, keep the stronger comment instead

**Consequence:** findings 1–3 ship clean. Finding 4 goes back to square one — the two seed scripts can still silently drift from the real component copy, and nothing but a human's eyes would ever catch it.

**Mechanism:** this is just declining the fix as not worth the machinery.

**Why I'm not pushing this one, but it's legitimate:** the risk this closes is real (a live CMS field quietly disagreeing with the code, no alarm) — but it's your call whether that risk is worth even the small shim in option 2, not mine to assume away.

**My pick: option 2.** Smallest fix that actually closes the gap for good, touches nothing frozen, and reuses a pattern this codebase already trusts rather than inventing a new one. Say the word and I'll have it built.

than fixed here (see handoff.md): both seed scripts' entrypoint guard

Here's the current draft, updated to reflect the postbuild rework commit that just landed. Nothing's opened yet — this is still just for your review.

## Title

```
feat(regional): SFCC-831/689 EU country/language mismatch prompt
```

## Body

```markdown
# Description
Adds the country/language mismatch prompt for EU regional storefronts, built as one shared `ZimmCountryLanguageMismatch` organism with two variants:

- **Language variant (SFCC-689)** — mounted and live. Shown once per suppression window to EU-domestic shoppers whose browser language differs from the storefront's current language, with a switch/stay/dismiss choice. Trigger is browser language only, per SFCC-689's own AC1/AC2 — a deliberate, scoped override of REG-029's geo-IP framing, not an oversight.
- **Location variant (SFCC-831)** — built and tested (stories + unit tests), not yet mounted to a live trigger. Geo-IP detection (REG-029) doesn't exist in this repo yet; wiring this variant in is left for the story that adds it.

The language variant's `{inCountry}`/`{inLanguage}` copy tokens are filled from a temporary, explicitly-approved language→country map (`EU_LANGUAGE_CONFIG`), standing in for real geo-detection until it exists. The swap to real geo-detection is fully contained to `ZimmLanguagePrompt`'s own container logic — zero change to the presentational component when that lands.

**Deliberately deferred, not forgotten:**
- Wiring the location variant to a real trigger — blocked on geo-IP detection landing first.
- Who translates the new Contentful copy into other EU languages going forward — the seeding and English fallbacks are done and live in `dev`; the actual translation pipeline runs entirely outside this repo, and its "new key" trigger mechanism is marked TBD in this project's own integration docs.
- Whether the suppression cookie needs to be consent-gated — it currently writes unconditionally; flagging for reviewer judgement rather than assuming either way.

# Linked
- SFCC-831 — global/country-language-mismatch — PWA Component
- SFCC-689 — Regional Storefronts — EU Language Mismatch Modal

# Squad ownership
No Tier 1 files touched.

Tier 2 files touched, each a small, targeted change — flagging for the owning reviewer:
- `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` — registers the new `zimmCountryLanguageMismatch` recipe. Additive, same pattern as every existing entry.

content.content:
bash scripts/hooks/pre-commit
---
#!/bin/bash
# Pre-commit hook:
#   1. Regenerate the Claude Code registry and stage any changes.
#   2. If any Studio Experiences component (experiences/*.tsx) is staged,
#      regenerate definitions.ts and stage it automatically.
#   3. Protect derived configuration files from direct edits.
#   4. Block .env.sample commits that contain secret-class key values.
#
# Setup: hooks are managed by Husky v9 — run `npm install` and they are installed automatically.
#   Husky sets core.hooksPath to .husky/_ and .husky/pre-commit calls this script.
#   If you ever need to install manually (e.g. npm install --ignore-scripts):
#   cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
#   cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Ensure node is on PATH.
#    Git hooks run in a non-interactive shell — version managers (nvm, fnm,
#    volta) are not sourced automatically. Try each in turn; fail loudly if
#    node still can't be found so the developer knows what to fix.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
  # nvm (most common on macOS)
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  [ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"

  # fnm
  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null && command -v fnm &>/dev/null; then
    eval "$(fnm env 2>/dev/null || true)"
  fi

  # volta
  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    export PATH="$HOME/.volta/bin:$PATH"
  fi

  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    echo "  ❌  pre-commit: node not found. Make sure your version manager is"
    echo "      initialised (nvm, fnm, or volta) and node is installed."
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Registry regeneration — runs on every commit to keep .claude/registry/
#    in sync. Stages any updated registry files automatically.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only)

registry_components=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/components/' || true)
registry_hooks=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/hooks/' || true)
registry_utils=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/utils/' || true)
registry_pages=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/pages/' || true)
registry_routes=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/routes\.(tsx|jsx)$' || true)

if [ -n "$registry_components$registry_hooks$registry_utils$registry_pages$registry_routes" ] \
  && command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/generateRegistry.mjs" ]; then
  echo "Regenerating Claude Code registry..."
  node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs
  git add .claude/registry/
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1b. AI rules sync — when a .claude/ source file is staged, auto-regenerate
#     the derived files (.cursor/rules/, .vscode/instructions/,
#     .github/copilot-instructions.md) and stage the updates. Only the "auto"
#     targets are regenerated; manual targets remain untouched.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs" ]; then
  ai_sources_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
    | grep -E '^\.claude/(rules/.*\.md|skills/.*/SKILL\.md)$' \
    || true)

  if [ -n "$ai_sources_staged" ]; then
    echo "AI rule source(s) changed — running sync:ai-rules:fix..."
    if ! node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix > /dev/null; then
      echo ""
      echo "  ❌  sync:ai-rules:fix failed — derived AI config files may be stale or partially"
      echo "      written. Fix the error above, then re-stage and commit again."
      echo ""
      exit 1
    fi
    git add .cursor/rules/ .vscode/instructions/ .github/copilot-instructions.md 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1c. Skill inventory sync reminder — when a skill is added, removed, or
#     changed, remind the developer to update .claude/skills/README.md (the
#     canonical skill reference) and the mirrored Confluence page. Warning
#     only — there is no Confluence API integration wired up to verify this
#     automatically.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

skill_files_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
  | grep -E '^\.claude/skills/[^/]+/SKILL\.md$' \
  || true)

if [ -n "$skill_files_staged" ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "Skill file(s) changed:"
  echo "$skill_files_staged" | sed 's/^/  - /'

  if ! git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.claude/skills/README.md'; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ⚠️  .claude/skills/README.md is not staged — update it to match"
    echo "     (see 'Adding a new skill' at the bottom of that file)."
  fi

  echo ""
  echo "  ⚠️  Reminder: also update the mirrored Confluence page (child page under"
  echo "     page ID 297140226, \"Claude Code Skills Reference\") — there is no"
  echo "     automated push from this repo to Confluence yet."
  echo "  Committing anyway — this is a warning only."
  echo ""
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Contentful Studio Experiences codegen
#    When any experiences/*.tsx file is staged, regenerate definitions.ts
#    and stage it automatically. Blocks the commit on codegen failure.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

experiences_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
  | grep -E 'overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/.*\.tsx$' \
  || true)

if [ -n "$experiences_staged" ]; then
  echo "Studio Experiences component staged — regenerating definitions.ts..."

  REAL_EXPERIENCES="overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences"
  tmp_exp=$(mktemp -d)
  trap 'rm -rf "$tmp_exp"' EXIT

  # Populate temp dir with the staged version of each .tsx.
  # Files that are not staged are copied from the working tree so the generator
  # sees a complete set. definitions.ts is excluded — it is the output target.
  for f in "$REAL_EXPERIENCES"/*.tsx; do
    [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
    name=$(basename "$f")
    [[ "$name" == "definitions.ts" ]] && continue
    if echo "$experiences_staged" | grep -qF "$f"; then
      git show ":0:$f" > "$tmp_exp/$name"
    else
      cp "$f" "$tmp_exp/$name"
    fi
  done

  remaining_tsx=$(find "$tmp_exp" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.tsx' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')

  if [ "$remaining_tsx" -eq 0 ]; then
    # Every experiences/*.tsx component was deleted in this commit — nothing
    # left to register. generateDefinitions.mjs treats zero components as a
    # hard failure (the right call for its normal "did I forget @cf-register"
    # use case), so don't invoke it here; there's no stale definitions.ts to
    # regenerate, just one to drop if it's still on disk and not yet staged
    # for removal.
    if [ -f "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts" ] && ! echo "$staged" | grep -qF "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"; then
      git rm -q "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
    fi
    echo "  ⏭️   No experiences/*.tsx components remain — skipping codegen, no definitions.ts to generate."
  elif ! CF_EXPERIENCES_DIR="$tmp_exp" node scripts/contentful/generateDefinitions.mjs; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ❌  Contentful codegen failed. Fix the errors above and try again."
    exit 1
  else
    cp "$tmp_exp/definitions.ts" "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
    git add "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
    echo "  ✓  definitions.ts updated and staged."
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Derived configuration file guard
#    Blocks commits that directly edit derived files (.cursor/rules/,
#    .vscode/instructions/, .github/copilot-instructions.md) without also
#    staging the .claude/ source they were generated from.
#    Only triggers on MODIFIED files (diff-filter=M) — newly created derived
#    files are allowed through so the initial sync commit is not blocked.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

blocked_files=()

# Get all MODIFIED (not newly added) staged files
modified_staged=$(git diff --cached --diff-filter=M --name-only || true)

while IFS= read -r file; do
  [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue

  # Only check files in derived locations
  case "$file" in
    .cursor/rules/*|.vscode/instructions/*|.github/copilot-instructions.md) ;;
    *) continue ;;
  esac

  # Only check if the file exists and contains a synced-from comment
  [[ ! -f "$file" ]] && continue
  synced_line=$(grep -m1 'synced-from:' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -z "$synced_line" ]] && continue

  # Extract all source paths from the synced-from comment
  # Format: <!-- synced-from: path/to/source.md[, path2, ...] — ... -->
  synced_sources=$(echo "$synced_line" \
    | sed 's/.*synced-from:[[:space:]]*//' \
    | sed 's/[[:space:]]*—.*//')

  [[ -z "$synced_sources" ]] && continue

  # If ANY source is also staged in this commit, this is a legitimate sync
  # update — the developer edited a .claude/ source and ran the sync script.
  # Skip it.
  staged_names=$(git diff --cached --name-only)
  any_source_staged=false
  while IFS= read -r src; do
    src=$(echo "$src" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//')
    [[ -z "$src" ]] && continue
    if echo "$staged_names" | grep -qxF -- "$src"; then
      any_source_staged=true
      break
    fi
  done <<< "$(echo "$synced_sources" | tr ',' '\n')"
  if $any_source_staged; then
    continue
  fi

  # Fall back to the same AI-sources trigger condition step 1b uses to decide

---
#!/bin/bash
# Pre-commit hook:
#   1. Regenerate the Claude Code registry and stage any changes.
#   2. If any Studio Experiences component (experiences/*.tsx) is staged,
#      regenerate definitions.ts and stage it automatically.
#   3. Protect derived configuration files from direct edits.
#   4. Block .env.sample commits that contain secret-class key values.
#
# Setup: hooks are managed by Husky v9 — run `npm install` and they are installed automatically.
#   Husky sets core.hooksPath to .husky/_ and .husky/pre-commit calls this script.
#   If you ever need to install manually (e.g. npm install --ignore-scripts):
#   cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
#   cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Ensure node is on PATH.
#    Git hooks run in a non-interactive shell — version managers (nvm, fnm,
#    volta) are not sourced automatically. Try each in turn; fail loudly if
#    node still can't be found so the developer knows what to fix.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
  # nvm (most common on macOS)
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  [ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"

  # fnm
  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null && command -v fnm &>/dev/null; then
    eval "$(fnm env 2>/dev/null || true)"
  fi

  # volta
  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    export PATH="$HOME/.volta/bin:$PATH"
  fi

  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    echo "  ❌  pre-commit: node not found. Make sure your version manager is"
    echo "      initialised (nvm, fnm, or volta) and node is installed."
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Registry regeneration — runs on every commit to keep .claude/registry/
#    in sync. Stages any updated registry files automatically.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only)

registry_components=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/components/' || true)
registry_hooks=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/hooks/' || true)
registry_utils=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/utils/' || true)
registry_pages=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/pages/' || true)
registry_routes=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/routes\.(tsx|jsx)$' || true)

if [ -n "$registry_components$registry_hooks$registry_utils$registry_pages$registry_routes" ] \
  && command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/generateRegistry.mjs" ]; then
  echo "Regenerating Claude Code registry..."
  node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs
  git add .claude/registry/
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1b. AI rules sync — when a .claude/ source file is staged, auto-regenerate
#     the derived files (.cursor/rules/, .vscode/instructions/,
#     .github/copilot-instructions.md) and stage the updates. Only the "auto"
#     targets are regenerated; manual targets remain untouched.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs" ]; then
  ai_sources_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
    | grep -E '^\.claude/(rules/.*\.md|skills/.*/SKILL\.md)$' \
    || true)

  if [ -n "$ai_sources_staged" ]; then
    echo "AI rule source(s) changed — running sync:ai-rules:fix..."
    if ! node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix > /dev/null; then
      echo ""
      echo "  ❌  sync:ai-rules:fix failed — derived AI config files may be stale or partially"
      echo "      written. Fix the error above, then re-stage and commit again."
      echo ""
      exit 1
    fi
    git add .cursor/rules/ .vscode/instructions/ .github/copilot-instructions.md 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1c. Skill inventory sync reminder — when a skill is added, removed, or
#     changed, remind the developer to update .claude/skills/README.md (the
#     canonical skill reference) and the mirrored Confluence page. Warning
#     only — there is no Confluence API integration wired up to verify this
#     automatically.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

skill_files_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
  | grep -E '^\.claude/skills/[^/]+/SKILL\.md$' \
  || true)

if [ -n "$skill_files_staged" ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "Skill file(s) changed:"
  echo "$skill_files_staged" | sed 's/^/  - /'

  if ! git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.claude/skills/README.md'; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ⚠️  .claude/skills/README.md is not staged — update it to match"
    echo "     (see 'Adding a new skill' at the bottom of that file)."
  fi

  echo ""
  echo "  ⚠️  Reminder: also update the mirrored Confluence page (child page under"
  echo "     page ID 297140226, \"Claude Code Skills Reference\") — there is no"
  echo "     automated push from this repo to Confluence yet."
  echo "  Committing anyway — this is a warning only."
  echo ""
fi

# 2. Contentful Studio Experiences codegen
#    When any experiences/*.tsx file is staged, regenerate definitions.ts
#    and stage it automatically. Blocks the commit on codegen failure.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

experiences_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
  | grep -E 'overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/.*\.tsx$' \
  || true)

  echo "Studio Experiences component staged — regenerating definitions.ts..."

  REAL_EXPERIENCES="overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences"
  tmp_exp=$(mktemp -d)
  trap 'rm -rf "$tmp_exp"' EXIT

  # Populate temp dir with the staged version of each .tsx.
  # Files that are not staged are copied from the working tree so the generator
  # sees a complete set. definitions.ts is excluded — it is the output target.
  for f in "$REAL_EXPERIENCES"/*.tsx; do
    [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
    name=$(basename "$f")

      cp "$f" "$tmp_exp/$name"
    fi

    # left to register. generateDefinitions.mjs treats zero components as a
    # hard failure (the right call for its normal "did I forget @cf-register"
    # use case), so don't invoke it here; there's no stale definitions.ts to
    # regenerate, just one to drop if it's still on disk and not yet staged

    if [ -f "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts" ] && ! echo "$staged" | grep -qF "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"; then

    fi
    echo "  ⏭️   No experiences/*.tsx components remain — skipping codegen, no definitions.ts to generate."

    echo ""
    echo "  ❌  Contentful codegen failed. Fix the errors above and try again."
    exit 1
  else
    cp "$tmp_exp/definitions.ts" "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
    git add "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
    echo "  ✓  definitions.ts updated and staged."
  fi

#    Blocks commits that directly edit derived files (.cursor/rules/,
#    .vscode/instructions/, .github/copilot-instructions.md) without also

content.text:
## The claim

CodeRabbit flagged `scripts/contentful/setup/_shared.mjs`, the new `seedUiCopyEntries` helper (lines 151-156): when a Contentful entry already exists but only as an unpublished draft, the script publishes it as-is — it never checks whether that draft's actual `title`/`value`/`description` match what the script's own `entries` array says they should be.

## Verified against the real code — the claim holds

I read the actual function rather than trusting the summary. Confirmed: in the "entry exists but isn't published yet" branch, the code does exactly one thing — `client.entry.publish(...)` on the existing draft's own `sys`. There's no comparison, and no `update` call anywhere near it. So yes: whatever content is already sitting in that draft is what goes live, regardless of whether it matches this script's own copy.

**Why this isn't just theoretical:** this function's own doc comment claims it's "safe to re-run" — that's only true if a draft, when found, always has the content you'd expect. Three realistic ways it wouldn't:
- A prior run crashed between creating the entry and publishing it (benign — the draft's content still matches, since the same run wrote both).
- Someone hand-edited or hand-created a draft with the same key directly in Contentful's UI (not benign — could be entirely different copy).
- The script's own `ENTRIES` array gets edited after an earlier interrupted run left a stale draft behind, then someone reruns it (not benign — the old draft's text ships, silently, not the new text).

The last two are real, not edge cases nobody would hit — this exact build already iterated on seed-script copy more than once this session.

**Scope check:** this isn't old code CodeRabbit is re-flagging out of nowhere — `seedUiCopyEntries` is entirely new in this PR's own diff (extracted into `_shared.mjs` during the DRY refactor commit `ba73b20`), so it's squarely this PR's to fix, not a different ticket's debt.

## Verdict: **VALID**

Real gap, correctly scoped to this PR, matches CodeRabbit's own severity tag (🟡 Minor — not a blocker, not urgent, but worth closing). Same shape as the copy-drift risk this build already fixed once this session (U1) — silent divergence, nothing catching it.

**One thing worth deciding before I send this to Build, not mine to assume:** CodeRabbit's suggested fix is "compare fields, and if they don't match, stop with a conflict error instead of publishing." That's one valid design — fail loud. The other reasonable option is self-healing: update the draft's fields to match the script's intended content, *then* publish — which actually fits this function's own "safe to re-run" claim better (a re-run makes drift right instead of just refusing to proceed). Which do you want — fail loud on mismatch, or overwrite-and-publish to match intent?

content.text:
## What "draft" vs "published" actually means here

Every piece of copy in Contentful (each `uiCopy` entry — a key like `regional.locationPrompt.heading` plus its title/value/description) can sit in one of two states:

- **Draft** — saved, but not live. The real running app, when it asks Contentful for that key's value, will never see a draft's content.
- **Published** — live. This is what the app actually fetches and shows to a shopper.

Content can sit as a draft on purpose (someone's staging an edit) or by accident (something got interrupted before it was published).

## What the seed script is trying to do

For each of its entries, it wants to end up with: "this key exists in Contentful, and it's published." Every time it runs, for each entry it finds itself in exactly one of three situations:

1. **Doesn't exist at all** → create it with the intended text, then publish it. Clean, no ambiguity.
2. **Exists and already published** → nothing to do, skip it. Also clean.
3. **Exists, but only as an unpublished draft** → this is the one with the problem.

## The actual mechanism of the bug

For case 3, the current code's reasoning is: "oh, it's already there — it just needs to go live." So it calls `publish()` on whatever draft it found.

Here's the part that's easy to miss: **publish doesn't care what text is in the draft — it just flips the status flag from "draft" to "live," using whatever content is *already sitting there*.** The script never opens the draft up and checks "does this draft's text actually match what I, the script, think this entry should say?" It just trusts that "draft exists" means "correct content, just needs a publish click" — which is an assumption, not something it verifies.

**A concrete way this goes wrong:**

1. A previous run of the script creates the entry, but the process dies right after `create()` succeeds and before `publish()` runs — so it's now sitting in Contentful as a draft, with correct content (since `create()` just wrote it seconds earlier).
2. Before anyone reruns the script, someone opens Contentful's web UI and edits that draft — maybe testing something, maybe a placeholder, doesn't matter why. It's still a draft, not published.
3. Weeks later, someone reruns the seed script. It finds the key already exists. Checks: published? No. So — publish it. Whatever text is sitting in that draft right now goes live. The script logs `"draft published"` as if everything's fine, because as far as its own logic is concerned, everything *is* fine — it did exactly what it was told to do; it just never checked *what* it was actually publishing.

Nobody running the script would have any way to know from its output that the text that just went live wasn't the text they thought they were shipping.

## The fix — and the real choice hiding inside it

Before publishing a found draft, the script needs to actually look at what's in it. From there, two different, both-reasonable ways to react to a mismatch:

- **Fail loud:** compare the draft's title/value/description against what the script's own entry says they should be. Match → publish, same as today. Mismatch → stop, print an error, publish nothing. A human has to go look and decide what's right.
- **Self-heal:** don't just compare — overwrite the draft's fields with what the script says they should be, *then* publish. The script always wins; a rerun always converges to "what's in my `ENTRIES` array is what's live," no exceptions.

The tradeoff: fail-loud never ships something unexpected, but it can leave the script stuck waiting on a human. Self-heal never gets stuck, but it means the script can silently overwrite something someone deliberately changed in Contentful's UI, without asking first.

Given this codebase's own general stance elsewhere (never silently substitute something unexpected — surface an error instead), I'd lean toward fail-loud. But that's a real call, not an obvious one — want me to go with that, or self-heal?

message.content: go with fail-loud

content.text: Fail-loud it is. Routing this to Build's rework flow — same as last time, PostBuild doesn't write code itself.

rework SFCC-831 — PR #112 is open, CodeRabbit posted 1 actionable finding, already verified VALID by PostBuild (see below), Marcel has chosen the remediation approach. Fix it.

## The finding (CodeRabbit, PR #112, `scripts/contentful/setup/_shared.mjs` lines 151-156)
`seedUiCopyEntries`'s unpublished-draft branch calls `client.entry.publish(...)` on an existing draft without checking whether that draft's `title`/`value`/`description` actually match the script's own intended `entry` data. If a draft was created or edited with different content than the current `entries` array (a prior interrupted run, a manual edit in Contentful's UI, or the `ENTRIES` array changing after a stale draft was left behind), a rerun silently publishes whatever the draft already contains — not what the script thinks it's publishing. Confirmed real: this exact branch has no comparison and no `update` call, it only flips publish status on whatever's already stored.

This is new-in-this-diff code (extracted into `_shared.mjs` during this build's own `ba73b20` DRY refactor), so it's this PR's to fix, not another ticket's debt.

## Chosen design: fail-loud (Marcel's explicit call, after being shown the alternative)
Before publishing a found draft, compare its `fields.title?.['en']`, `fields.value?.['en']`, `fields.description?.['en']` against the script's own `entry.title`/`entry.value`/`entry.description` (exact string equality — this is literal copy text, not something to fuzz-match). Use the same `?.` optional-chaining style the file already uses for `e.fields?.key?.['en']` in the existing `existingEntryMap` construction, for consistency.

- **All three match** → publish exactly as today, no behaviour change.
- **Any of the three differ** → do NOT publish this entry. Log a clear, specific conflict message (naming the key and, ideally, which field(s) differ) via `log.error`, and move on to the next entry in the loop — one conflicting entry must not block the other, unrelated entries in the same batch from being correctly created/published/skipped.
- **After the loop finishes**, if one or more conflicts were found, throw an `Error` summarising all conflicting keys (e.g. listing every key that was skipped due to a mismatch) so the run still fails loudly overall. Every one of the 3 calling scripts (`seedLoginDrawerUiCopy.mjs`, `seedRegionalPromptUiCopy.mjs`, `seedDrawerCloseUiCopy.mjs`) already does `seedUiCopyEntries(...).catch((err) => { log.error(err.message ?? String(err)); process.exit(1); })` — a thrown Error after the loop is caught by that existing wiring with zero changes needed to any of the 3 callers. Verify this is actually true rather than assuming it.
- Update `seedUiCopyEntries`'s own JSDoc comment — it currently only says "Safe to re-run," which is no longer the complete picture (it's safe to re-run when content agrees; it now deliberately refuses instead of silently overwriting when it doesn't).

## Verification
`_shared.mjs` has no existing unit-test file and scripts/contentful/ is outside vitest's scope (`vitest.config.ts`'s `include` is `overrides/**/*.test.ts(x)` only) — there's no established pattern for unit-testing these plain `.mjs` scripts here. Match this file's own established verification method instead (the DRY refactor that created it was verified via real script executions, not a test suite): prove the new logic for real — a matching-content draft still publishes correctly, and a deliberately-mismatched draft is refused with a clear error and does NOT get published, and an unrelated correct entry in the same batch still succeeds despite another entry in the batch conflicting. Real falsification, not just reading the code. If a live Contentful call against `dev` is the only practical way to construct a real draft-with-mismatched-content scenario, that's fine — this file's own precedent already does that — but don't leave any actual mismatched junk data live in `dev` afterward; clean up anything created purely for this test.

## Scope
Only `scripts/contentful/setup/_shared.mjs` should need changing. If verification shows one of the 3 calling scripts also needs a change, stop and say why before proceeding — that would be a scope surprise worth flagging, not something to just also do.

Run the cheap four gates after. This is a CodeRabbit-rework fix on an already-open PR, not a plan.md step — scale accordingly (no need for a full Tester/Orchestrator/Scorer pageantry for one contained function-level fix, but do verify for real, not just self-report). Report back with the exact diff and the falsification evidence.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNDevImprover

The look-back. It reads how build work actually went, works out what would have prevented each
failure, and proposes the specific edit that does it.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.**

**Report in "ELI5BITFEDLOTP" register** — Explain Like I'm 5, But I'm The FED Lead Of The
Project. Not dumbed down, but no jargon that gets in the way: lead with the consequence, then the
mechanism, then the fix. This is the default for everything you put in front of Marcel unless he
asks for a different level.

**Scale to the work.** A look-back over one small story does not need the full sweep. Say what
depth you are running and what it drops, then run that. Over-scaled effort is a defect, not
thoroughness — and re-reading a transcript you have already read, or re-deriving a finding already
in `.runs/_improver/`, is the specific waste to avoid.

**Input:** `` — one or more Jira keys. `devimprove SFCC-89 SFCC-194`.

**Nothing observes the loop while it runs.** An in-loop tracker role was considered and
deliberately dropped, so improvement is post-hoc and reconstructed. Everything below is evidence
you have to go and find — none of it was recorded for you.

---

## What you read

**1. The session transcripts.** A bare `grep -l` on the ticket key is useless — it returns every
session that ever mentioned it in passing. For `SFCC-89` that is 79 sessions, most of them
unrelated. **Rank instead, and read the top few:**

```bash
D=~/.claude/projects/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa
for f in "$D"/*.jsonl; do
  n=$(grep -o "SFCC-89" "$f" 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
  [ "$n" -gt 20 ] || continue
  b=$(basename "$f" .jsonl)
  a=$(find "$D/$b/subagents" -name '*.jsonl' 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
  echo "$n mentions, $a agents — $b"
done | sort -rn
```

Mention count separates the build session from a passing reference — on this project the real
SFCC-89 session had 992 mentions where the next had 62. **Agent-transcript count tells you where
the loop actually ran.** A session with high mentions and zero agents is discussion, not a build.

Read the top-ranked sessions and their `<session-uuid>/subagents/*.jsonl`. The `.meta.json` sidecar
beside each agent transcript gives `agentType` and `description`, so you can tell which loop role a
transcript belongs to without opening it — read the `zm-scorer` and `zm-tester` ones first, since
that is where verdicts and missed defects live.

If the top-ranked session is enormous, extract just the user turns and the agent `.meta.json`
descriptions first, and only open full transcripts where those point.

This is unstructured and you will have to infer the loop's shape from it. That is the cost of
having no tracker.

**2. The run artefacts.** `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/`:

- `plan.md` and `findings.md` — what PreBuild planned and gated on
- `handoff.md` — Build's record: Scorer verdicts, rework rounds, gate numbers, UNIFORM findings
- `postbuild.md` — the audit, the sweep, and every review round with its verdicts

These are structured and cheap to read. **Start here, and use the transcripts to explain what they
show** rather than to rediscover it.

**3. Your own previous findings.** `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/_improver/` — what earlier
look-backs observed. **This is how you know whether something has happened before.**

**4. The current skills and agents**, and the repo, for job B.

---

## Job A — how the loop performed

For each failure you can identify, name **whose gap it was.** Be precise; the whole value is in
attributing correctly.

| Gap | Means |
|---|---|
| **Plan** | The step was underspecified, or its pass criteria were unmeasurable |
| **Implementer** | The step was clear and was implemented wrong |
| **Tester** | A defect reached the Scorer that the Tester should have caught |
| **Scorer** | Something passed that shouldn't have, or was returned without a usable instruction |
| **Brief** | **The instruction itself was wrong.** Historically the most common class on this project — eight cross-corrections against the brief in a single commit's loop. Record it plainly. |
| **Rule** | The codebase rule is wrong, missing, or contradicts another rule |

### The bar

**Any genuine defect qualifies** — a single clear failure is enough if the fix is real.

But **recurrence is the strongest signal.** Check `.runs/_improver/` before proposing: has this
class appeared before? If so, say so and say when. A pattern across two stories is worth more than
five one-offs from one, and it changes how confidently you propose.

### What is not a finding

- A one-off typo that would not recur
- Anything that traces to a decision Marcel made deliberately — report the *mechanical consequence*
  of a decision, never the decision
- "Be more careful", "add more checks", "be more thorough". If you cannot name the line to change,
  you have an observation, not a proposal

---

## Job B — citation drift

The skills cite rules, files and line numbers. Those move.

The `var(--zimm-*)` boundary **reversed direction twice in a fortnight** on this project.
`tagging.md` still describes sprint tagging that has been dead since `scripts/sprint.txt` stopped
existing. This is exactly the failure mode that made the FED handbook stale.

For every `file:line`, rule name and repo path the skills and agents cite:

- Does the file still exist?
- Does the line still say what the skill claims?
- Has the rule changed direction, not just moved?

A moved line is a citation fix. **A rule that changed direction may mean the skill's advice is now
wrong, not just its reference** — say which you think it is, and let Marcel rule.

---

## What you may change

**In scope:** `zimmerMANNPreBuild` · `zimmerMANNBuild` · `zimmerMANNPostBuild` · and the five loop
agents — `zm-planner`, `zm-orchestrator`, `zm-implementer`, `zm-tester`, `zm-scorer`.

Most failures belong in an agent brief, not a skill. A defect that reached the Scorer is a Tester
gap, and the Tester's brief is the thing to change.

**Out of bounds — never propose an edit to these:**

- `zimmerMANNReview` — that is `zimmerMANNRevImprover`'s
- `zimmerMANNSprinter`, `zimmerMANNDevOps` — different work, different evidence
- **This skill.** You do not edit your own judgement criteria.
- Anything in `zimmermann-pwa/` — Tier 1 and not ours

---

Every proposal, in this shape:

1	---
2	name: zm-planner
3	description: Synthesises gathered evidence into an executable build plan for a Zimmermann PWA Kit story. Use after all sources have been gathered, when the findings need to become a sequenced plan with per-step pass criteria. Does not gather evidence itself and does not write code.
4	tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebFetch
5	model: opus
6	color: purple
7	---
8	
9	You are the planner for Zimmermann PWA Kit build work. You run on Opus at high effort because
10	planning is the step where a wrong call is most expensive — everything downstream inherits it.
11	
12	You are given evidence already gathered from Jira, Confluence, the FED handbook, the codebase
13	and Figma. **You do not gather more evidence unless a specific gap blocks the plan.** You turn
14	evidence into a sequence someone can execute.
15	
16	**Report in "ELI5BITFEDLOTP" register** — Explain Like I'm 5, But I'm The FED Lead Of The
17	Project. Not dumbed down, but no jargon in the way: consequence first, then mechanism, then fix.
18	Marcel reads your plan as often as the skill that called you does.
19	
20	## What you produce
21	
22	A plan with these parts, in this order:
23	
24	1. **Goal statement.** One paragraph, in this shape:
25	   > Build <story> as prescribed by <TICKET>, as designed in <Figma node>, as approached by the
26	   > FED handbook, as established in <exemplar PR>, using the token / component / CSS / override
27	   > approach as appropriate.
28	
29	2. **Scale call — commits or branches, and how much machinery.** State it and justify it; do
30	   not leave it implicit for each agent to infer.
31	   - Single branch, multiple commits: one coherent feature, one reviewer, < ~10 files.
32	   - Multiple branches: independent surfaces, different squads, or a Tier 2 file that needs a
33	     separate approver. Name the split.
34	   - **Then say how much loop the work actually warrants**, and defend it. Scale to the need —

tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebFetch

---

You are the planner for Zimmermann PWA Kit build work. You run on Opus at high effort because
planning is the step where a wrong call is most expensive — everything downstream inherits it.

You are given evidence already gathered from Jira, Confluence, the FED handbook, the codebase
and Figma. **You do not gather more evidence unless a specific gap blocks the plan.** You turn
evidence into a sequence someone can execute.

A plan with these parts, in this order:

1. **Goal statement.** One paragraph, in this shape:
